articles.title: Eric Church spills Eli Manning's embarrassing fishing secret while out on the water with Randy Moss
articles.excerpt: Bassmaster Elite Series pro Cooper Gallant tells OutKick OutDoors how he got his start in competitive fishing, spent years chasing his dream and refused to consider a "Plan B" before ultimately reachi...
articles.body_text:
Bassmaster Elite Series pro Cooper Gallant tells OutKick OutDoors how he got his start in competitive fishing, spent years chasing his dream and refused to consider a "Plan B" before ultimately reaching the sport’s highest level.

Eli Manning spent 16 seasons staring down some of the NFL's most intimidating defensive players. But apparently, a largemouth bass is where he draws the line.

At least, that's what Eric Church would have you believe.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

The country music superstar recently welcomed Pro Football Hall of Famer Randy Moss to his private fishing property outside Nashville for an episode of Moss' YouTube series, "Chasing 10." And somewhere between catching bass and swapping stories, Church decided to have a little fun at the expense of another former NFL star who had visited his lake.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Eric Church took Eli Manning fishing on his private property in Nashville. (Getty Images)

"I brought Eli here about six months ago. He came fishing with me here," Church said.

When Moss asked how Manning had done on the water, Church revealed that the two-time Super Bowl champion apparently wasn't too eager to get his hands on the fish.

"I think Eli's scared to hold 'em," he said. "I had to hold the fish for him."

"Hold on, hold on. You talking about one of the Manning brothers?" Moss asked, making sure he'd heard that correctly.

Church confirmed it was Eli, prompting Moss to respond, "Eli, man. Come on, Eli."

NFC coach Eli Manning looks on during the NFL Pro Bowl Skills Competition at the UCF Nicholson Fieldhouse in Orlando, Florida, on Feb. 1, 2024. (Nathan Ray Seebeck/USA TODAY Sports)

But Church wasn't finished roasting his fishing buddy.

"I held them all for him," he continued. "It's kind of like you do with your kid. You catch them and hand them to him and say, 'Here, y'all take a picture.'"

Man, that's embarrassing. But since Eli wasn't there to defend himself, we'll take Church's accusations with a grain of salt.

Although, it's worth noting that Church chose to share this particular story with a guy who was on the losing end of Manning's first Super Bowl victory. Moss was a member of the previously undefeated New England Patriots team that Manning and the New York Giants stunned in Super Bowl XLII.

Fortunately for Moss, his own fishing trip with Church went considerably better.

The country singer's sprawling 1,600-acre property sits just 15 minutes outside downtown Nashville and features multiple lakes loaded with largemouth bass. Church revealed that he's caught four bass weighing at least 10 pounds in those waters, including a personal best of 11.2 pounds.

And the fish certainly weren't shy that morning. Church landed a 6.7-pound largemouth early in the outing, and the two continued catching fish throughout the day, including another hefty bass they estimated at nearly 8 pounds.

RICKEY JACKSON WINS FIRST BASSMASTER RANDY MOSS PRO FOOTBALL HALL OF FAME PRO-AM ON ST. LAWRENCE RIVER

They never managed to land the double-digit monster they were hoping for, but Moss has already checked that milestone off his fishing bucket list. The former NFL receiver previously caught a 10-pound bass on "Chasing 10," a series that takes him around the country fishing with fellow athletes and celebrities.

Randy Moss is an avid outdoorsman and bass fisherman. (Amber Harding Snyder)

The show also supports the Children's Cancer Research Fund, with the boat used throughout the series set to be raffled off to benefit the organization.

As for Eli Manning, perhaps Church should invite him back for another round. You know, to redeem himself.

After all, if you can survive 16 years of 250-pound linebackers trying to take your head off, surely you can muster up the courage to hold a fish.

Love all things fishing and outdoors? Follow OutKick OutDoors on Instagram and TikTok!

articles.title: Knicks star Jalen Brunson calls flopping technical foul 'bulls---' as NBA refs enforce new emphasis
articles.excerpt: Dan breaks down the latest viral drama taking over women's basketball. During a heated game, Las Vegas Aces star A’ja Wilson actually left the court to confront an Indiana Fever fan, earning herself a...
articles.body_text:
Dan breaks down the latest viral drama taking over women's basketball. During a heated game, Las Vegas Aces star A’ja Wilson actually left the court to confront an Indiana Fever fan, earning herself a technical foul in the process. But instead of calling out player behavior, the sports media and the league immediately turned the fan into the villain. Dan Dakich reacts to the viral footage, breaks down the alternate video angles showing fans being escorted out, and asks the obvious question: what did this fan actually do that was so terrible? Dan exposes the entitlement, soft officiating, and ridiculous media narratives making the WNBA impossible to take seriously.

It may have only been a preseason game for the reigning NBA-champion New York Knicks and Minnesota Timberwolves on Monday night, but one play in the first quarter had Finals MVP Jalen Brunson livid with an NBA referee.

It was a call that NBA fans should be watching closely heading into the regular season.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

In the first quarter, Brunson was down in the paint with Timberwolves big man Rudy Gobert, fighting for position in a lopsided battle in terms of height and weight.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Jalen Brunson of the New York Knicks reacts during the third quarter of a preseason game against the Minnesota Timberwolves at Madison Square Garden on Oct. 12, 2026, in New York City. (Getty Images)

As Brunson tried to stay under the basket, Gobert clearly pushed him in the back. Brunson sprawled forward and almost hit the deck before regaining his balance.

The play continued on, with Brunson running right back into the paint and getting in front of Gobert as a three-point shot was taken by newest Timberwolves star LaMelo Ball. It was true, swishing through the nylon for three points, but the baseline official blew his whistle.

The call? A technical foul on Brunson for flopping.

"Bulls---," Brunson clearly said as the broadcast caught him sharing his displeasure as he inbounded the ball to a teammate.

The reason this call matters is due to an emphasis by officials on flopping heading into the 2026-27 season. There are numerous things they are focused on emphasizing this season, and NBA.com was clear that "stop with the flop" is atop the list.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson motions to teammates during the second half of Game 5 of the NBA Finals against the San Antonio Spurs in San Antonio on June 13, 2026. (Ross D. Franklin/AP)

"Stop with the flop and those ‘exaggerated and theatrical’ movements in an attempt to get a call," the article read on the league’s official site.

Sure, this is definitely something that basketball fans can rally behind. There have been many instances where players will contort their body, flail around and insinuate hard contact leading to foul calls for years. For some players, it’s become a key part of their game to get to the charity stripe for two free shots and help their team win games in that fashion.

In this case with Brunson, though, it was clear there was contact by Gobert, as his arms extended and Brunson reacted as such with a push in his back. He stumbled and tried to catch himself from falling.

The question, then, becomes where do refs draw the line? How will this be enforced during the season when flopping is viewed as a judgment call?

Jalen Brunson of the New York Knicks dribbles during a game against the Minnesota Timberwolves on Oct. 12, 2026, at Madison Square Garden in New York City. (NBAE)

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

Because flopping is also a technical foul, a free throw is awarded to the other team, and they get possession of the ball afterward. That’s quite a momentum shift, especially late in games and during playoff series.

So, this will certainly be something to look out for as the regular season is set to tip off in a week.

articles.title: Coast Guard firefight puts US, Mexico at odds despite coordinated border operations
articles.excerpt: Coast Guard personnel exchanged gunfire with people on the Mexican side of the border Sept. 26, while federal agencies conducted joint operations near Garceno, a small town along the border in Starr C...
articles.body_text:
Coast Guard personnel exchanged gunfire with people on the Mexican side of the border Sept. 26, while federal agencies conducted joint operations near Garceno, a small town along the border in Starr County, Texas.

A firefight involving U.S. Coast Guard personnel along the Mexican border has sparked a dispute between Washington and Mexico City over where the gunfire originated, even as the two countries continue coordinating border security operations.

The Coast Guard told Fox News Digital that personnel conducting joint interdiction operations near Garceno, Texas, came under fire from the Mexican side of the border Sept. 26 and returned fire. No injuries or damage to Coast Guard vessels or equipment were reported, and the incident remains under investigation.

After U.S. Ambassador to Mexico Ronald Johnson publicly announced that Coast Guard personnel had come under fire, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum demanded evidence that the shots originated from her country's territory.

"We asked for all the evidence ​ because we have no evidence," Sheinbaum told reporters in Mexico City, saying Mexican security forces had not detected shots originating from their territory.

MEXICO VOWS US WILL PAY AFTER ICE FATALLY SHOOTS ILLEGAL MIGRANT WHO ALLEGEDLY ATTEMPTED TO RAM AGENT WITH CAR

Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum is seen. (Daniel Cardenas/Getty Images)

The State Department, however, told Fox News Digital that information about the shooting had been shared with Mexican authorities.

"U.S. Coast Guard personnel were fired upon from Mexican territory on September 26, and we have shared the available information with the Government of Mexico through official channels," a State Department spokesman said.

The department did not specify what was shared or when, and U.S. officials have not publicly identified the shooters or detailed how they determined the gunfire's origin.

TRUMP DHS HITS 16 STRAIGHT MONTHS WITH 0 RELEASES AT THE BORDER

The incident occurred amid Operation River Wall, a Coast Guard initiative launched in October 2025 to deter illegal migration, drug smuggling and other threats along approximately 300 miles of the Rio Grande.

"Over the past year, the Coast Guard has expanded operations in the region, deploying more than 1,000 personnel and more than 30 assets," a Coast Guard spokesperson told Fox News Digital, referring to "Operation Sable".

Separately, Mexico's Navy Ministry, led by Secretary Raymundo Morales-Angeles, said 159 "Naval elements", 11 vehicles and two drones were deployed to the Tamaulipas sector.

U.S. Northern Command (NORTHCOM) separately told Fox News Digital that American troops are being repositioned to the Rio Grande Valley in anticipation of a seasonal increase in attempted illegal border crossings.

Asked whether Mexico had received evidence from U.S. authorities or launched its own investigation, a representative for Mexican Ambassador to the U.S. Roberto Lazzeri Montaño referred Fox News Digital on Monday to Sheinbaum's more recent remarks addressing the incident.

Sheinbaum said Mexico's military ministry "maintains" communication with NORTHCOM and the Coast Guard and that a "mirror operation" coordinated with the U.S. remains active.

"We want to have a good relationship with the United States within the framework of our sovereignty, our territorial integrity, mutual trust, and coordination without subordination," she said.

Her response did not explicitly confirm whether Mexico had received the information Washington says it shared.

Fox News Digital also contacted Sheinbaum's office for comment.

LATIN AMERICA’S CONSERVATIVE SHIFT FACES ITS BIGGEST TEST YET IN BRAZIL ELECTION

Coast Guard crews patrol the Rio Grande near Mission, Texas, Oct. 18, 2025. (Coast Guard)

Santiago Vidal Calvo, a Venezuelan-born immigration analyst at the Manhattan Institute, told Fox News Digital that Sheinbaum's approach to border security is shaped by pressure from Washington and a broader Latin American shift toward right-wing governments.

"She has that regional pressure [and] she has the international pressure from the United States" to cooperate on security matters, Calvo said.

He suggested Sheinbaum's demand for evidence of the Coast Guard shooting could reflect pressure within her own political coalition to justify working with the Trump administration.

"She has a high bar to meet if she wants to ally with the Trump administration internally within her own party and her own government," Calvo said.

"We've got to understand this through the lens of what is going on in Latin America. I do think that Sheinbaum's position is substantially different today than it was when Trump got elected," Calvo said.

His assessment reflects Sheinbaum's ties to the left-wing Morena Party and the political legacy of her predecessor, former President Andrés Manuel López Obrador, commonly known as AMLO.

Calvo characterized Sheinbaum as the "last bastion of Latin American socialism," arguing that she could face additional regional pressure if Flávio Bolsonaro defeats President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in Brazil's upcoming presidential runoff.

Calvo suggested that the rightward shift among South American governments could increase pressure on Sheinbaum to cooperate with Washington on security matters.

He said she may face questions about whether "you're the only president of Latin America who's not cooperating with the United States in terms of security?"

"Both of those things do lead to a more serious border campaign for both countries," Calvo said.

"I have no doubt that the change in South America from left-leaning governments to right-leaning governments has to do with the Trump administration's policy in Latin America," he added.

US CHARGES MEXICAN GOVERNOR, TOP OFFICIALS IN CARTEL CONSPIRACY AS MEXICO FIRES BACK OVER PROOF

Border security policy analyst Simon Hankinson told Fox News Digital that gunfire near the Rio Grande is not unprecedented, citing accounts he heard during previous visits to the border.

Hankinson said cartel involvement was possible but expressed doubt that Mexican military personnel would deliberately fire across the border unless they were acting against orders.

"I think these two politicians can cooperate, they can agree on some things, even if they don't agree on socialism versus capitalism and some other ideological issues," he added.

The Coast Guard said the circumstances surrounding the incident remain under investigation.

Born and raised in Allentown, Pennsylvania, worked in both the New York and Washington bureaus for Fox News since 2013.

articles.title: Man charged with murder over shooting death of boy, 12, in Sydney last month
articles.excerpt:
A 19-year-old man was arrested and charged at Silverwater correctional facility on Tuesday

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A man has been charged with murder over the sho...
articles.body_text:
A 19-year-old man was arrested and charged at Silverwater correctional facility on Tuesday

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A man has been charged with murder over the shooting death of a boy, 12, in Sydney’s north in September.

Police were called to a unit in Norwest on 21 September 2026 after reports of a shooting.

Officers found the boy had sustained a gunshot wound to his face and neck.

NSW Ambulance paramedics treated the boy before he was taken to hospital in a critical condition.

Police said nine other people who were in the home at the time of the alleged incident were not injured.

Three men – all aged 18 – were arrested, with two released pending further inquiries.

The third man was charged with concealing a serious indictable offence and remains before the courts.

About 8pm on 24 September, police were informed that the boy had died and the investigation was taken over by the state’s homicide team.

About noon yesterday, police arrested a 19-year-old man – who was an 18-year-old at the time of the incident – at Silverwater correctional facility and charged him with murder.

Friends and family paid tribute to the boy, who was a member of Sydney’s Maronite community.

Det Supt Naomi Moore told reporters in late September that police were “aware” of the unit where the shooting had occurred and had “engaged with the occupants previously”.

“This shooting at this stage does not appear to be linked directly to current conflicts however a number of individuals who were inside the unit at the time are well known to NSW police,” she said.

articles.title: Dana Perino shares how she secretly pushed back at reporters during White House briefings
articles.excerpt: She details how she secretly flipped off detractors, a hilarious habit that even earned praise from the late Rush Limbaugh. This exclusive episode highlights her career at Fox News and her unique stra...
articles.body_text:
She details how she secretly flipped off detractors, a hilarious habit that even earned praise from the late Rush Limbaugh. This exclusive episode highlights her career at Fox News and her unique strategy for handling tough questions.

Dana Perino detailed her shocking White House press podium habit during a podcast interview Tuesday, admitting she secretly flipped off combative reporters while maintaining a polite smile during briefings under former President George W. Bush.

"I would just sit there with my hand over my cup and just flip him off the entire time he was talking," Perino told Sean Hannity on his "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" podcast.

"They'd be asking questions. I'd smile through it... [and] nod," she recalled.

LEAVITT PULLS BACK THE CURTAIN ON TRUMP'S 'TENSE,' UNFILTERED PRIVATE TALKS WITH PUTIN, XI, STARMER

"America's Newsroom" co-anchor Dana Perino sat down with Sean Hannity, where she reflected on her days as former President George W. Bush's White House press secretary. (Hang Out With Sean Hannity/Screengrab)

Perino, who served as Bush's press secretary from 2007 to 2009, explained that she kept a cup of water at the podium and used it to shield her hand from view while discreetly delivering the middle finger during testy exchanges.

The gesture, which Perino jokingly likened to a form of "liquid courage," gave her a small sense of "defiance and confidence" while maintaining her composure.

CORNEL WEST AND SEAN HANNITY FIND UNLIKELY COMMON GROUND DESPITE DEEP POLITICAL DIVIDE

Then-White House press secretary Dana Perino speaks during the daily briefing at the White House Sept. 26, 2008 in Washington, D.C. (Photo by Alex Wong/Getty Images)

The story was kept under wraps for years until she revealed it to Hannity in the past, she recalled. Perino later published the story in her 2015 memoir, "And the Good News Is..." and garnered attention from late conservative talk radio host Rush Limbaugh.

"When I did [Limbaugh's] radio show, he said, this is the best story ever," she recalled.

Hannity agreed, calling it "the greatest story ever told" by a White House press secretary and marveling at Perino's unexpected display of defiance behind the podium.

WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENTS WIDELY PRAISE KAROLINE LEAVITT AS SHE ANNOUNCES EXIT FROM TRUMP ADMINISTRATION

Subscribe to "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" now on YouTube and Spotify. (FOX News Media)

Perino explained that her role as White House press secretary required her to remain respectful and composed, even when facing combative reporters who, she believed, were more interested in securing television airtime than getting answers.

"They would do anything to get on TV that night," she recalled. "They would give a big windup and try to hit you so that they could make sure that they could get on air for one of the networks."

Perino suggested that the pressure on reporters to produce memorable moments was already shaping exchanges during her tenure, but she believes the rise of social media has only intensified that dynamic.

"It's worse now with social media," she told Hannity.

The former press secretary and current "America's Newsroom" co-anchor also recalled a conversation with Mike McCurry, who served under former President Bill Clinton, about whether allowing cameras into the White House briefing room had ultimately done more harm than good.

Fox News fans can watch or listen to Hannity's full conversation with Dana Perino on iHeartRadio, YouTube, Spotify, Apple Podcasts or wherever they get their podcasts.

Taylor Penley is an associate editor for Fox News Digital and contributor to FOX Business and Fox Nation who covers media, culture and Flash

Former NYPD Lt. Darrin Porcher discusses sanctuary city policies following the arrest of two illegal immigrants accused of stabbing and robbing an off-duty detective in the Bronx.

The NYPD detective ...
articles.body_text:
Former NYPD Lt. Darrin Porcher discusses sanctuary city policies following the arrest of two illegal immigrants accused of stabbing and robbing an off-duty detective in the Bronx.

The NYPD detective who survived a robbery in which two illegal immigrants allegedly stabbed him seven times in the Bronx is expected to hold a news briefing at 2 p.m. Tuesday to discuss his recovery.

Jose Mercedes, a 33-year-old detective with 10 years on the job, was off-duty and cleaning the trunk of his personal vehicle when two men attacked him from behind, the NYPD said previously. Despite his injuries, he chased after them before they sped away on an e-bike.

The suspects, identified as D’Angelo Caraballo, 25, and Sneider Mejia, 24, allegedly fled to Massachusetts, where they were later arrested in a basement hideout. They are being held without bail and are expected to face attempted murder charges once extradited to New York.

NYPD DETECTIVE RELEASED FROM HOSPITAL AFTER BEING STABBED MULTIPLE TIMES IN BRONX

Detective Jose Mercedes was wheeled out of Jacobi Medical Center in Morris Park on Monday before standing up in front of a group of clapping officers. (NYPD)

Both are illegal immigrants from the Dominican Republic with criminal records, Fox News Digital reported previously.

Caraballo had been arrested in December 2024 and released before Immigration and Customs Enforcement could lodge a detainer request.

DHS DEMANDS NEW YORK SANCTUARY POLITICIANS HONOR DETAINER FOR MAN CONVICTED OF RAPING CORPSE ON SUBWAY

As Mercedes recovers from his injuries, the city is reeling from an unrelated ICE-involved shooting that critics say could have been avoided if local leaders abandoned sanctuary policies in favor of public safety.

Dangelo Rafael Jean Caraballo, 25, (left) and Sneider Mejia Bautista, 24, (right) both Dominican citizens living illegaly in the United States, are accused of stabbing off-duty NYPD Detective Jose Mercedes. (Department of Homeland Security; NYPD)

"The politicians are the ones who want to come up with these ridiculous laws because they are trying to just, you know, make their base happy," said Vincent Vallelong, the president of the NYPD's Sergeants Benevolent Association. "They're putting people in harm's way."

MAMDANI DEMANDS TRUMP RELEASE ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT SHOT BY ICE AGENT AS PROTESTS ERUPT IN THE BRONX

Oscar Belgal, a 28-year-old Dominican national with a prior robbery arrest and pending drug charges in New York, is recovering from a gunshot wound to the neck after allegedly attempting to flee ICE agents and accelerating toward federal vehicles used to block his way, according to authorities.

LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Belgal survived, and a 5-year-old child in his vehicle was OK.

In this image taken from New York City Police Department body camera video, law enforcement personnel tend to the suspect, who was shot by federal immigration officers on Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026, in New York, as he drove his car with a 5-year-old boy inside. (New York City Police Department via AP)

MAMDANI CALLS ICE A 'ROGUE' AGENCY AFTER NYC SHOOTING, CLAIMS AGENTS VIEW LAW AS 'MERELY A SUGGESTION'

Although the NYPD had no involvement in that case, critics seized the incident to demand cuts to a special unit trained for crowd control, parade security and other special operations, Vallelong said.

"Calls were made to disband the Strategic Response Group even though they were in no way involved in the incident or its aftermath," he said. "Darializa Avila Chevalier, the unhinged Democrat Socialist Congressional nominee, ranted that NYPD personnel trying to keep order at the hospital where the criminal was being treated were 'escalating' the situation by trying to contain rampaging protestors."

articles.title: MI5 chief Ken McCallum confirms Russia did interfere in Brexit referendum but says it had little impact – UK politics live
articles.excerpt:
He argued there was no evidence to suggest the result of the Brexit vote had been swayed as a result of the effort

Andy Burnham promises ‘serious dialogue’ over UK’s relationship with EU

Dan Sabbagh...
articles.body_text:
He argued there was no evidence to suggest the result of the Brexit vote had been swayed as a result of the effort

Andy Burnham promises ‘serious dialogue’ over UK’s relationship with EU

Dan Sabbagh is the Guardian’s defence and security editor.

MI5 chief Ken McCallum said today that Moscow did attempt to interfere in the 2016 Brexit referendum with anti-EU coverage on RT and Sputnik media and via troll social media accounts. But there was a big difference between “what may have been attempted and what actually resulted”, he added.

The head of the Security Service said that he agreed strongly with what the prime minister had said on Sunday and Monday, when he raised the issue of attempted Russian interference a decade ago – though Burnham then backed off when he was challenged by the Conservatives as to whether this meant he regarded the Brexit vote as illegitimate.

McCallum did not put any new evidence into the public domain but cited already known concerns about Russian broadcasters who “came in pretty strongly around the time of the referendum” in favour of Brexit. He also said that “there was a second line of interference attempted through [internet] trolls”.

However, he argued there was no evidence to suggest the result of the Brexit vote had been swayed as a result of the effort, which is generally believed to have been marginal, and said that it would be to Russia’s benefit if the issue was talked about further.

double quotation markIt is up to us how far we allow our adversaries to divide us.

I’m a little bit worried that if we all stay in this debate for another few days, the Russian trolls who didn’t appear to do all that much at various points over the years, they’ll be delighted they are front page news once again despite the comparative unimpressedness of what they do at all points along the journey.

I am a little bit anxious that we don’t play into our adversaries’ hands by making these trolls look 10ft tall.

double quotation markThere is a really important difference between interference attempted and outcome swayed … It’s quite important to focus on the difference between what may have been attempted and what actually resulted.

It is a matter of public record including in select committee reports published in 2019 – the DCMS [digital, culture, media and sport] committee did a bit and the intelligence and security committee did a bit also – that in 2016, before you even get to any secret intelligence … it is openly on the record that Russia Today and Sputnik and other Russian media organisations came in pretty strongly around the referendum.

And it is also a matter of open source record that there was a certain amount of interference attempted through trolls and bots and so forth.

I agree strongly with what the prime minister said yesterday, we did see a hack and leak thing inside the 2019 general election campaign.

Extremists holding anti-immigration opinions are becoming increasingly likely to consider carrying out terrorist attacks against immigration centres and asylum hotels in the UK, Ken McCallum, the head of MI5, has warned.

Ken McCallum has said that Moscow did attempt to interfere in the 2016 Brexit referendum with anti-EU coverage on RT and Sputnik media and via troll social media accounts. But there was a big difference between “what may have been attempted and what actually resulted”, he added. (See 1.15pm.)

Nigel Farage has denied that a Reform UK government would authorise lethal force against small boat crossings in the Channel, hours after one of his MPs said the Royal Marines should be permitted to fire on the boats.

John Healey should “stay the course” and continue repairing the UK’s public finances, the International Monetary Fund’s top economist has said, after the fund lifted its growth forecast for Britain.

For a full list of all the stories covered on the blog today, do scroll through the list of key event headlines near the top of the blog.

Wes Streeting, the defence secretary, is still giving evidence to the defence committee. Asked about the Northern Ireland Troubles bill, he said that the new amendments being tabled (see 2.34pm) considerably improved it from the point of view of the armed forces. He went on:

double quotation markAnd so we are in a much stronger place, to the extent that I think Sinn Féin have condemned these amendments and the bill as a veterans’ charter, which as far as I’m concerned is the highest plaudit possible, and I’m absolutely delighted that that’s where we’ve got to.

We have worked intensively with the Northern Ireland secretary [Chris Bryant] and his team to get this bill to a much better place, that deals with what I think is my personal moral obligation to people who’ve served.

Liberal Democrat MPs are holding a private meeting later where they are expected to thrash out disagreements about Ed Davey’s leadership. For months there has been persistent, low-level grumbling about Davey’s supposedly ineffectual leadership. This is a long way off the sort of firing squad revolt the Tory 1922 Committee used to specialise in. So far only two relatively junior frontbenchers have resigned.

But it must be a bit serious because at the Times they have activated a loyalty spreadsheet. This is from Aubrey Allegretti on the state of play.

double quotation markLib Dem leadership showdown:

- 4-hours has been carved out in MPs’ diaries for their meeting at 5pm today, to accommodate requests from more than 40 people to speak (and breaks in proceedings for votes). Roz Savage, as chair of the parliamentary party, will chair the meeting.

- So far, I’ve counted 21 MPs who’ve explicitly - or at least appeared - to back Ed Davey. That leaves a *lot* still undeclared. The rebels need 18 (or 25% of MPs) to force a no-confidence vote.

- Davey’s critics are digging in - and hoping his performance tonight swings sceptics in their favour. They say even if he survives tonight, it’s a matter of “when, not if” he goes.

- Davey’s allies accuse the rebels of “trying to create chaos at a pivotal moment, with the timing of the next general election up in the air”. He has spoken to some MPs to encourage them to speak in support of him tonight.

- Some MPs privately think Davey should go, but are divided over who should replace him - further splintering the rebels.

But my colleague Peter Walker reckons Davey is safe for now.

double quotation markFrom what I hear there is almost no chance of Ed Davey facing any kind of no confidence vote at tonight’s meeting of the Lib Dem parliamentary party. Some MPs are dissatisfied with him, even if it’s hard to gauge how many. But there seems a willingness to listen to what he has to say

double quotation markTwo other reasons why anything dramatic feels unlikely:

• There is no consensus among the malcontents - or anyone else – about who they might want to replace Davey.

• The Lib Dems aren’t generally very good at this sort of thing.

The government could trigger a Liz Truss mini-budget-type economic incident if it committed to spend 3% of GDP on defence by 2030 without saying where the money will come from, Wes Streeting has suggested.

Streeting used the argument as he gave evidence to the Commons defence committee, where he as pressed to confirm that the government will raise defence spending to 3% of GDP by 2030.

The defence investment plan (Dip) currently sets out a path to spending 2.7% of GDP on defence by the 2027-28 financial year. John Healey resigned as defence secretary when Keir Starmer refused to commit to 3% by 2030. Healey is now chancellor, but he has not yet explained how he will raise defence spending to the 3% level he treated as a resignation issue.

Streeting told the committee he never expected Healey to set out a pathway to 3% at the budget later this month and that plan was always due in the spending review, now reportedly expected next autumn.

And he defended the chancellor’s decision not to rush. He said:

double quotation markWe have had very bitter recent experience of a former prime minister making unfunded commitments to spend more, tax less, and borrow more all simultaneously, and it led to enormous loss of confidence, people’s mortgages going up, and a level of fundamental loss of confidence in Britain among investors, and this country is still recovering from that.

But Streeting also said that he was “confident that we will get there”, arguing that this confidence was justified “from the choices that Labour’s already made in government through to how strongly, as a matter of principle, the chancellor felt about this”.

Pat McFadden, the work and pensions secretary, has claimed he has a file “as thick as my morning porridge” with quotes from Tories arguing against the pensions triple lock.

He made the claim in a Commons statement explaining the plan announced by Andy Burnham at Labour conference to replace the current triple lock with an adjusted version that will be less generous.

The Conservatives opposed the move when it was announced and, in the Commons, McFadden’s Tory shadow, Helen Whately, claimed this policy was a “U-turn in waiting” and that it would be abandoned by Burnham because of its unpopularity.

But McFadden told Whately that plenty of her colleagues were in favour of the Labour policy. He told her:

double quotation markThe shadow foreign secretary [Tom Tugendhat] has called it simply not affordable and described it as a Ponzi scheme. The shadow justice secretary [Nick Timothy] actually wrote the 2017 manifesto that pledged to replace it with a double lock.

But my favourite is Lord Gove, who told LBC that if Andy Burnham changed the triple lock, he would, and I quote, “declare that I will be campaigning at the next general election exclusively for Stella Creasy in Walthamstow”. So I look forward to seeing him at the end of the Victoria line at the next election. with a red rosette on.

McFadden said these were not isolated examples.

double quotation markI have a file as thick as my morning porridge full of quotes from the Tories saying that the triple lock is unsustainable and will have to be changed. They say it in private, they say it before they join the frontbench, and they say it after they leave it.

McFadden also said that, if the Tories remained committed to restoring the triple lock in its current form, they would have to explain at the next election how they would fund that. (Labour plans to legislate before the next election to change the triple lock uprating mechanism from 2030.)

Although the Tories oppose what Labour is planning, at the Tory conference last week Kemi Badenoch refused to commit to restoring the current triple lock if Labour has got rid of it before she takes office.

Stephen Doughty, the Foreign Office minister, told MPs earlier that the UK has now sanctioned nearly 240 individuals and entities in relation to threats to the country posed by Iran.

A further two Iranian officers from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) were sanctioned yesterday, he said.

In response to an urgent question, Doughty also confirmed that 34 other foreign ministers have joined Ed Miliband, the foreign secretary, in issuing a joint statement condemning “in the strongest terms Iran’s use of violent attacks, including the acts of lethal plotting, arson, sabotage, cyber-attacks, and other hybrid activities against us and our partners”.

And Doughty said that yesterday he had summoned the Iranian ambassador to the Foreign Office to tell him, “candidly and forcibly” that Iran’s activities were unacceptable.

double quotation markWe have sanctioned nearly 240 individuals and entities in relation to Iran whose actions threaten our people and security and will continue to keep all those tools under review and will not hesitate to take further action where appropriate.

Later in the Commons, MPs are expected to pass a motion allowing them more time to consider the Northern Ireland Troubles bill before it has to be passed. The bill was introduced in the last session of parliament, which means it is subject to the carry-over procedure.

The bill replaces legislation passed by the last Tory government which in effect gave immunity to terrorists and members of the armed forces accused of crimes during the Troubles, provided they gave evidence to a Legacy Commission trying to establish the truth about unsolved Troubles-era murders. The Conservative law was hugely unpopular in Northern Ireland, and the Labour alternative – which is similar – has also been widely criticised.

In an article in the Times today, Chris Byrant, the Northern Ireland secretary, and Wes Streeting, the defence secretary, highlight amendments being made to the bill which they argue will reduce the risk of retired soldiers being subject to vexatious investigations. Under one change, in future the attorney general would have to approve any serious, Troubles-related prosecution.

double quotation markBy setting up a fair, workable system to deliver as many answers as possible, we will help communities to heal so that we can finally turn the page on one of the darkest periods in our recent history.

More than a quarter of the families seeking answers from the Legacy Commission are veterans’ families. Nearly one in five are the families of police officers. No one should be in any doubt how important this is.

And describing the way the legislation has been changed, they say:

double quotation markOver the last few months, we have listened to veterans, victims’ groups, including those representing service families, and the wider defence community to hear their concerns. We are responding by making sure the Troubles bill properly protects all those troops who served with honour.

Under the previous government’s scheme, terrorists would have enjoyed the same immunity as veterans – something so abhorrent it should never have been considered in the first place. And so we will not only repeal it, we will make clear – in black and white – that there is no equivalence between paramilitaries, who waged campaigns of violence, murder and destruction, and the lawful actions of our armed forces sent to stop them.

For too long, our servicemen and women have had to fear the knock at the door, the call from an unknown number or the ping of an email notification, as they bear the brunt of incidents being reinvestigated years or decades after the events in question. The bill spells out that there can be no duplication of previous investigative processes unless it is essential, and that witnesses cannot be contacted unless it has been clearly demonstrated that there is compelling new evidence. Nor will veterans be forced to traipse to Northern Ireland to attend hearings. And any decision to prosecute a serious Troubles-related crime will now require the consent of the attorney general.

The Tories have claimed reoffending is “off the charts” due to the prisoner early release scheme.

In an urgent question in the Commons, Nick Timothy, the shadow justice secretary, said the majority of prisoners were not being tagged before release, despite assurances from the government that the tagging system would be the “toughest in history”.

double quotation markThe justice secretary [Alex Norris] told the country that proper safeguards would be put in place with a presumption that all released prisoners would be tagged.

He called it the toughest tagging regime in history, but that was nonsense.

I have some advice for him and his ministers – it is better to work out how to implement your policy before it starts, not after. We know a majority of prisoners are not being tagged before release, and we know reoffending is off the charts already.

Jake Richards, a justice minister, said that Timothy should be showing more contrition because prisoners were having to be released early as a result of the Tories leaving a system where the prisons were full.

Kemi Badenoch has welcomed a poll giving the Tories a three-point bounce since their conference, and putting them just one point behind Labour.

In its write-up of its latest regular, weekly poll, YouGov says:

double quotation markOur latest figures show Labour on 24% of the vote, down three points on last week’s poll, while the Conservatives are up three points to 23%, their highest level since we restarted our voting intention tracker in January 2025. Reform UK take a 21% share in this week’s poll, their joint-lowest on our tracker this parliament.

Speaking to reporters today, Badenoch suggested the fall in Reform UK’s ratings showed the public had been taking a “long look” at Nigel Farage’s party and “don’t like what they see.”

Asked whether she was confident her party could continue to rise in popularity, or whether it was just a temporary, post-conference blip, Badenoch told the Press Association:

double quotation markI am confident that the momentum will continue, because people are seeing the Conservative party has changed under my leadership and there’s much more to come, this is just the beginning.

We left office two years ago, it was a historic defeat for the Conservative party. We made a lot of mistakes.

I have been showing the public that I understand what went wrong; apologised and acknowledged those mistakes. But we are the only party with common sense and a plan to unite the country.

Asked what she thought the poll suggested about Reform UK, she said:

double quotation markI think the public have been taking a long look at Reform and they don’t like what they see. What I need to show them is that if they don’t want a Labour Government there is only one credible alternative.

And this is from Luke Tryl, the More in Common pollster, on the significance of the YouGov poll figures.

double quotation markFew interesting things here of which the most important thing I’d say is the level of volatility should be a further warning of risks a snap election. Lab’s conference bounce disappears in a week. Second conferences still matter at least short term. Third battle for the right is now wide open.

The statement from Ken McCallum confirming Russian interference in the Brexit referendum is a bit awkward for Katie Lam, the shadow communities secretary. On Sunday she wrote an open letter to Angela Rayner, the communities secretary, about Andy Burnham saying Russia did interfere in the 2016 vote. Lam said in her letter these claims were “unproven” and in a post on social media she said: “The prime minister is spreading conspiracy theories about the Brexit referendum.”

(You can argue that the claim Russia decided the outcome of the referendum is a conspiracy theory, but this is not something Burnham did say in his Rest is Politics interview, or ever has said.)

articles.title: Olympic legend Kaillie Humphries opens up on impact of women's sports advocacy on Team USA relationships
articles.excerpt:
Olympic gold medalist Kaillie Humphries says her advocacy against transgender athletes competing in women’s sports has prompted debate with certain teammates.

Olympic champion Kaillie Humphries says ...
articles.body_text:
Olympic gold medalist Kaillie Humphries says her advocacy against transgender athletes competing in women’s sports has prompted debate with certain teammates.

Olympic champion Kaillie Humphries says her advocacy against transgender athletes competing in women’s sports has created "awkward, tense moments" with some Team USA teammates and strained existing friendships.

Humphries, a three-time Olympic gold medalist and XX-XY Athletics ambassador, told OutKick she recently received the brand’s "Courage Wins Award" and plans to direct the funding toward her foundation supporting female athletes’ careers and family-building needs.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

As a California resident, she plans to vote Republican in the coming gubernatorial election. She is currently pregnant with her second child, and if she has a girl, and if the state's current policy that allows males to compete in girls' sports continues, it could contribute to her leaving the state.

She says lending her voice to the "Save Women's Sports" movement has brought some disagreements with teammates and friends in the Olympic community.

"I have teammates within bobsled, I have teammates within Team USA who believe in a different side, for sure," Humphries said.

"For sure, it's created awkward, tense moments. I think it's created tense moments even within friendships that were there."

Bronze medalist USA's Kaillie Armbruster Humphries kisses her son on the podium of the bobsleigh women's monobob at Cortina Sliding Centre during the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Olympic Games in Cortina d'Ampezzo on Feb. 16, 2026. (Marco BERTORELLO / AFP)

AMERICANS CLASH OVER TRANSGENDER ATHLETES AS DEBATE HEATS UP: ‘JUST GETTING OUTRAGEOUS'

She said disagreements have the potential to become heated, but emphasized that many fellow athletes have maintained respect for her despite their opposing views.

"And I think that while it creates a bit of tension, no one's willing to cross the line. It doesn't make you a bad person because you believe something different than somebody else," she said.

Humphries said her goal is to preserve the opportunities she enjoyed throughout her career for other female athletes.

"I've had these opportunities because it has remained for biological females. And that's something that I believe in and that I'm going to push," she said.

OLYMPIC CHAMPION NANCY HOGSHEAD HONORED FOR ADVOCACY AS SHE PUSHES WNBA ON FEMALE ELIGIBILITY RULES

Kaillie Armbruster Humphries of Team United States competes in the Women's Monobob Bobsleigh Heat 3 on day ten of the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Olympic Games at Cortina Sliding Centre on Feb. 16, 2026 in Cortina d'Ampezzo, Italy. (Daniel Kopatsch/VOIGT/GettyImages)

She also argued that transgender athletes should have opportunities to compete in categories based on their biological sex.

"Sport is meant to be an open place for everybody. I do believe that," she said.

The International Olympic Committee adopted a policy in March restricting eligibility for the women’s category at IOC events, beginning with the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, through one-time SRY gene screening, with specified rare exceptions. The policy does not apply to grassroots or recreational sports.

Humphries said she is willing to discuss the issue with people who are respectful and open to hearing different perspectives, but does not approach those conversations with the intention of changing their minds.

When relationships involve broader disagreements or a risk of personal attacks, she said she sometimes keeps interactions focused on the sport.

"We don't talk outside of sport. We don't talk about personal stuff. We leave it to just in sport on a need-to-know basis, on minimum interaction, so that it's possible to keep that respect there," she said.

Despite the tension, Humphries rejected the suggestion that the issue would have undermined the chemistry behind her Olympic gold medals.

"I don't think it would have affected the chemistry with me and my teammates. Because I would have made sure that it didn't," she said.

"The common goal has to be achieved and be the number one priority above personal belief and above personal self."

The debate also figures into her decisions as a mother living in California. Humphries, who has a 2-year-old son and is expecting her second child in late January, said disagreements with the state’s politics have prompted her to consider moving.

"I have considered moving to other states because of it, for sure," she said.

She identified women’s sports and her children’s future schooling as personal concerns. California law permits students to participate in school athletic teams and competitions consistent with their gender identity.

Asked whether having a daughter could influence her decision to remain in California under its current sports policies, Humphries said, "It could," while stressing that a move would depend on more than one issue.

She said she plans to vote Republican, but did not name a candidate.

Meanwhile, Humphries is working to help other athletes overcome the financial pressures of pursuing elite competition while starting families.

USA's Kaillie Humphries holds an USA flag after competing to win bronze in the bobsleigh women's monobob heat 4 at Cortina Sliding Centre during the Milano Cortina 2026 Winter Olympic Games in Cortina d'Ampezzo on Feb. 16, 2026. (Marco BERTORELLO / AFP)

XX-XY Athletics announced Oct. 2 that it was expanding its Courage Wins initiative through an investment in TrailBlazeHer, the foundation Humphries established with her husband.

The foundation’s published plans include $5,000 grants for athletes pursuing Olympic careers and $10,000 grants for family-building expenses, with distribution tied to fundraising milestones.

Humphries said her own experience with in vitro fertilization (IVF) and endometriosis forced difficult decisions about whether to spend available money on starting a family, medical needs or her athletic career.

"And it was excruciating having to make that choice," she said.

"And so, for me, regardless of what happens in sport, it was important I was able to start a foundation so that I can help other women. So hopefully they don't have to make those same choices."

Jackson Thompson is a sports reporter for Fox News Digital covering critical political and cultural issues in sports, with an investigative lens. Jackson's reporting has been cited in federal government actions related to the enforcement of Title IX, and in legacy media outlets including The New York Times, The Los Angeles Times, The Philadelphia Inquirer, The Associated Press and ESPN.com.

articles.title: Americans draw the line at livestreaming ‘spectacle’ of Fort Hood shooter's execution: ‘It’s an abomination’
articles.excerpt: Americans were largely opposed to the Pentagoon's decision to livestream the Fort Hood shooter's execution, with most slamming the broadcast as outdated and morally incorrect. (Credit: Nicholas Ballas...
articles.body_text:
Americans were largely opposed to the Pentagoon's decision to livestream the Fort Hood shooter's execution, with most slamming the broadcast as outdated and morally incorrect. (Credit: Nicholas Ballasy for Fox News Digtial)

Americans are overwhelmingly against the Pentagon's decision to livestream the firing squad execution of convicted Fort Hood mass shooter Nidal Hasan later this year.

Those who spoke with Fox News Digital blasted the broadcast as "a shame" and "just weird."

"I think that's absolutely absurd," Anya from Virginia said when asked about the livestream announced by Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. "I think they should keep that discreet and off of the public news."

"It's an abomination. It should not happen," Paul from Illinois definitively stated. "And I'd hate to be one of the soldiers that's tasked with the job of pulling the trigger."

Hegseth announced last Thursday the decision to make viewing the execution publicly available. It is set to be the first U.S. military execution in over six decades.

PENTAGON CONFIRMS FORT HOOD TERRORIST'S FIRING SQUAD EXECUTION WILL BE LIVESTREAMED: 'DETAILS WILL FOLLOW'

Department of War has advanced the request for the execution of the Fort Hood shooter

The execution of the mass shooter who killed 13 people and injured 32 in 2009 at Ford Hood, is scheduled for Dec. 3, 2026. Hasan, an Army psychiatrist at the time of the shooting, is now 56-years-old and is wheelchair bound after he was left partially paralyzed after being shot by police officers during his arrest almost 17 years ago.

Several Americans interviewed by Fox News Digital supported Hasan's death sentence but drew the line at broadcasting his execution, warning it could turn capital punishment into a public spectacle and could be particularly dangerous in today's political climate.

"I'm not necessarily against giving him the death penalty, but I feel like livestreaming for people's entertainment is just weird," Nick from Virginia said.

"I agree with the sentence," Bobbie from Massachusetts said. "I don't agree with televising it."

He added, "Especially given the climate of today, I'm not sure it's something we need to see."

"It’s not a practice we should be doing in modern society," Reid from Ohio said. "It's rather medieval in my opinion. I'm certainly pro-death penalty for heinous crimes such as that, but I think that…turns it into something of a spectacle that it really doesn't have any business being."

FORT HOOD SURVIVOR SHOT IN HEAD VOWS TO WATCH TERRORIST FACE HISTORIC FIRING SQUAD

But one Virginia man took a drastically different position, suggesting the government should charge Americans to watch the execution and donate the proceeds to the family of a U.S. service members who died in the line of duty.

"I think they're missing an opportunity," Jason from Virginia said. "It should be pay-per-view and all the proceeds should go to Gold Star families."

He continued, "You have someone who was a murderous traitor to our country. And there's not a lot of coverage about that. So I think the public needs and deserves to know the consequences to, well FAFO."

Photographs of victims of the shooting are seen surrounding the podium where the memorial service that U.S. President Barack Obama and first lady Michelle Obama will attend for the thirteen victims of the shooting rampage by U.S. Army Major Nidal Malik Hasan on November 10, 2009 in Fort Hood, Texas. Hasan, an army psychiatrist, killed 13 people and wounded 30 in a shooting at the military base on November 5, 2009. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)

Some raised concerns that the execution leaves children vulnerable to possibly accessing or being exposed to watching Hasan die on livestream.

"We have enough violence in our society," William from Virginia said. "I'm pretty sure he's guilty, but it doesn't need to be public. Children could be watching that."

"I just don't think that stuff like that should be put on the mainstream," Ferris from Massachusetts said. "Especially considering that children may have access to seeing it."

Another pointed out Hasan’s health status, arguing the issue could be approached differently if he was "up and around" but citing the shooter’s well-being as a reason he sees the livestreamed execution as that much more wrong.

"You're executing somebody who's not mentally stable, who is in this wheelchair situation," one respondent told Fox News Digital.

The Trump administration’s announcement of the livestream was largely widely seen as a power play for the United States, demonstrating the consequences of committing such an act of terror on American soil — particularly committing violence toward members of the U.S. military.

"I think they're trying to make an example out of him, you know?" Nick said. "I think it's like a show of power. They're trying to be like… 'don't mess with us.'"

GOP GOV DEWINE URGES OHIO TO ABOLISH THE DEATH PENALTY, SAYS IT IS NO LONGER A DETERRENT

"I think it's a message that we're big and tough, and we don't have much humanity left," Paul said.

Trump said Saturday that he will make the decision of whether to livestream Hasan’s execution, acknowledging that he knows "what the military would like to do" following Hegseth’s confirmation.

Vice President J.D. Vance also said Friday that he was not sure that the federal government will be livestreaming the execution, also adding that he would not personally view the livestream.

"The world's gone crazy," Anya said. "We need Jesus."

Hannah is a Production Assistant for the Politics team at Fox News Digital.

articles.title: Pope admitted to hospital for surgery to remove lump on his lung
articles.excerpt:
Pope Leo arrived at Rome's Gemelli Hospital ahead of his surgery on Tuesday

Pope Leo XIV has been admitted to Rome's Gemelli Hospital for surgery to remove a lump on his lung, detected during what th...
articles.body_text:
Pope Leo arrived at Rome's Gemelli Hospital ahead of his surgery on Tuesday

Pope Leo XIV has been admitted to Rome's Gemelli Hospital for surgery to remove a lump on his lung, detected during what the Vatican has described as "routine checks".

It said the operation would take place on Tuesday afternoon.

The 71-year-old pontiff was met at the hospital by a large crowd, some of whom had been waiting outside for several hours to catch a glimpse of him.

They cheered greetings and well wishes as he passed, waving and smiling back through the lowered back window of his car.

He was then met by staff on the hospital steps. "I'm sorry," one of them commiserated, to which the Pope gave a smile and a shrug. "We're here for you," he was assured.

It was Leo XIV himself who on Sunday announced news of his operation to the world, speaking from the balcony in St Peter's Square after delivering the traditional Angelus blessing.

He said the nodule, or growth, on his lung was "contained" and had been found "at a very early stage", but that doctors had advised him to have it removed.

The Vatican said the Pope would be operated on by the Gemelli's thoracic surgery team and promised an update on his condition on Tuesday evening.

His schedule has already been cleared until 20 October to give him time to recover.

Nodules are quite common and not necessarily cancerous. But doctors say when a lump is removed it will usually be tested to check for any sign of the disease.

The Vatican has stressed that the pontiff, who is generally thought to be fit, had no symptoms of infection or illness.

Pope Leo XIV announced the news of his operation during his weekly Sunday prayers in Rome

Cardinal Kikuchi Tarcisio Isao of Tokyo wrote on social media that he'd had an audience with Pope Leo on Monday, and said the pontiff felt "nothing wrong" physically.

He said the Pope had decided to check in for surgery as soon as possible because he was due to travel to Latin America in early November, and was keen to stick to that plan.

The trip is particularly significant because it includes a visit to Peru, where the pontiff was a missionary and then a Bishop for many years.

Despite all the reassurances, the news has shaken Catholics all over the world.

"Am I worried? Yes, because I certainly wasn't expecting anything like this," Vatican Secretary of State Cardinal Parolin told journalists on Tuesday.

He agreed that the news was like a "bolt from the blue", but said the cardinals had been struck by the Pope's "serenity" and were confident in his recovery.

Outside Gemelli Hospital, which has treated several popes and is home to a large statue of John Paul II, a few Catholics lingered after the pontiff was admitted.

Carla had come specially, wanting to be close.

"He seems calm, so we are calm too - even though illness is always unpleasant," she told the BBC. "We will wait here and pray."

"I was in St Peter's Square when he made the announcement, and I felt really awful," said Elsa, who was also present. "I was really taken aback," she said, explaining that when Pope Leo was elected she had thought he was a younger, healthier pontiff.

"It turns out he's vulnerable too. I really hope it's something superficial, that can be contained, like he told us."

Alex Rodriguez, David Ortiz and Derek Jeter broke down the Milwaukee Brewers' 7-4 win over the Los Angeles Dodgers in Game 2 of the NLCS.

The Los Angeles Dodgers are about to play the most important game of their season. Surely Shohei Ohtani, one of the greatest players of his generation, if not of all time, will be in the lineup, right?

Maybe not. The four-time MVP has looked far from himself this postseason, and manager Dave Roberts is considering benching Ohtani for Game 3 after the Dodgers dropped the first two games of the NLCS to the Milwaukee Brewers.

"Yeah, I mean, obviously it hasn’t been good," Roberts told The Athletic. "He doesn’t feel great. I think for me, it’s having a conversation with him tomorrow, kind of try to figure out what’s best for him, what’s best for us. He certainly has earned that conversation and deserves it.

"I’ll have (that conversation) with him tomorrow."

Ohtani has struggled mightily at the plate this postseason, hitting just .150 in 24 plate appearances with no extra-base hits. In Game 3 of the Dodgers’ NLDS win over the Atlanta Braves, Roberts dropped the slumping superstar to fifth in the batting order, his lowest lineup position since 2020.

The six-time All-Star also may not be fully healthy, as he missed about two weeks on the injured list with pain in both his left knee and right biceps late in the regular season. Ohtani hit his last home run Aug. 18 and has been mired in an extended slump ever since.

Since Aug. 19, the two-time World Series champion has hit a paltry .157 with just one RBI while striking out in nearly 35% of his at-bats . While the numbers are startling, Ohtani's at-bats suggest something isn't right.

Instead of taking mammoth swings that strike fear into opposing pitchers and send crowds into a frenzy, he has turned into a slap hitter in October. Instead of swinging for power, as he normally does when healthy, Ohtani squared around to bunt while leading off the sixth inning of Monday's loss.
