Europe has emerged as a key market because it offers organisations higher profit margins than the US. Since the beginning of the decade, European police have confiscated more drugs than American forces, and data indicates that Europe now represents about a quarter of global consumption.

Europol recently reported that out of 731 MTCNs operating across Europe, 149 are connected to Latin American organisations. Of these, 67 have Latin American members, and 22 mainly consist of Latin Americans.

articles.title: Bacon, eggs and Bowie: how year 12 English students tackled ‘human strength and vulnerability’ in HSC paper
articles.excerpt:
Tens of thousands of high school students across New South Wales sit the first test of their final exams

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

“How does the composer of your pr...
articles.body_text:
Tens of thousands of high school students across New South Wales sit the first test of their final exams

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

“How does the composer of your prescribed text offer you opportunities to examine assumptions about human strength and vulnerability?”

This was the bamboozling English question tens of thousands of year 12 students sat down to answer on the first day of their final school exams.

Kayden Tran, 18, had a “really great breakfast” of rice, bacon and eggs – but was it enough to get through an essay exploring tenacity and sensitivity in the writings of Tim Winton, George Orwell or Malala Yousafza?

“This morning, I felt extremely stressed and I kind of gave up hope,” the student of Canley Vale high school in Sydney’s west told the Guardian.

“But after doing the exam, I feel perfectly fine, I feel content, like I did the best I possibly could,” he said after the HSC English 1 paper on Tuesday.

Mary Alnimry listened to the song Heroes by the late David Bowie to prepare.

“I discovered that song through an assessment for year 10 and, every time, before every English exam, I listen to that song and it just reminds me of English,” she said.

The pair was among about 200 Canley Vale students to sit the test, just one cohort in the roughly 75,000 students across New South Wales working to wrap up their high school careers.

“You just have to go in and believe that you know the content,” Alnimry, 17, said. “That’s how I felt in the morning. And then after the exam, obviously it’s really rewarding. I completed everything, but there’s always that curiosity lingering.

“I think that it was pretty fair, there was nothing out of the ordinary.”

On Reddit, other year 12 students weren’t as confident.

“Honestly I think that’ll kick most people in the ass, the fact the question had so much to unpack I personally found it hard to address it all, I focused on vulnerability and strength and sprinkled a bit of assumptions,” one student with the handle bberson wrote on Tuesday afternoon.

Another, djungleskog41, was concerned they skipped over parts of the question: “I did Orwell too and tbh I didn’t address the question at all. I only focused on how like human vulnerability and weakness forces us to submit into the regime and rebelling is a sign of human strength blah blah blah but i barely mentioned my assumption so im rlly upset about that lol.”

Alana Miller, an English teacher at Canley Vale high school, has shepherded 17 years of year 12 students through the exams. She said the nerves don’t stop with students, and she too woke up this morning with the year 12s on her mind.

“We care so much about the students, we spend so much time,” she said. “We want them to do well, we want them to feel particularly that these exams are something they could achieve in.”

Fantasy books have been a growing hit at Canley Vale high alongside Japanese manga. Miller said she’s spent the past year trying to meet students where they are to help engage the next generation of readers.

“I think the best way is to … talk to them about books, shows, films that they might see,” Miller said. “I think choosing engaging texts in the classroom can be a huge stepping stone for resistant readers. … I just try and tell them they haven’t met the book yet that will get them to love reading.”

“I’m feeling not too bad, because I did finish everything,” the 17-year-old said. “I don’t know if I answered the questions fully as I should’ve. You just have to trust yourself with how much work you put in and that you actually remember it. I trust in myself.”

Effie Niarchos, the principal of Canley Vale high, said the HSC represented a rite of passage for year 12s, marking the past six years of high school and the next chapter in their lives.

“All of the teaching, all the learning is building towards this moment,” she said. “We want them to be ready for the world, and we look at it as we’ve achieved something to be able to successfully prepare them for this moment”.

She said students have been experiencing a bit more anxiety in recent years, possibly from community expectations, possibly from the world shifting underneath kids’ feet.

But as she saw off the last of those who sat for the exam on Tuesday, she looked back with a smile and a sense of pride.

HSC results will be released on 16 December.

articles.title: US military archbishop urges Catholic soldiers to refuse involvement in Army firing squad execution
articles.excerpt: Fox News chief national security correspondent Jennifer Griffin examines the history and use of firing squads in the United States and discusses the debate over plans to livestream the execution of Fo...
articles.body_text:
Fox News chief national security correspondent Jennifer Griffin examines the history and use of firing squads in the United States and discusses the debate over plans to livestream the execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan. She also looks at Vice President JD Vance’s concerns about live-streaming the execution on ‘Special Report.’

Catholics serving in the Army should request to be excused from participating in the planned firing squad execution of a convicted Fort Hood mass shooter, which the Pentagon has proposed livestreaming, a prominent U.S. archbishop who oversees Catholic pastoral services for the military said on Monday.

Archbishop Timothy Broglio raised several objections to the Pentagon's unprecedented plan to broadcast the execution of Nidal Malik Hasan, a former Army psychiatrist who was convicted of killing 13 people and wounding 32 others in a 2009 shooting at the Fort Hood military base. Hasan, now 56, uses a wheelchair, after being shot by responding officers during the attack.

Hasan is set to be executed at Fort Hood on Dec. 3, at 1 p.m. CST, according to the U.S. Army, which would make him the first person to be executed by firing squad by the U.S. military since 1945. It would also mark the first U.S. military execution by any method since 1961. Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth said he wanted soldiers to execute Hasan at the time, day of the week and location of the shooting and has argued that making the execution public would help serve as a deterrent.

Broglio recalled presiding over the funeral of one of Hasan's victims, Michael Grant Cahill, the only civilian killed in that attack, and expressed sorrow over the deadly shooting. But the archbishop questioned whether the U.S. government wanted to "imitate the terrorists of this world and make a public spectacle of barbarically killing our adversaries."

POPE LEO DENOUNCES DEATH PENALTY AS 'INADMISSIBLE' AHEAD OF PENTAGON'S PLANNED LIVESTREAMED EXECUTION

Archbishop Timothy Broglio raised several objections to the Pentagon's unprecedented plan to broadcast the execution of Nidal Malik Hasan. (AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough)

Hasan's crime "was heinous, but does exposing the public to his execution serve any purpose?" Broglio asked in a statement.

"I oblige any Catholics assigned to the firing squad to request to be excused from this action contrary to the teaching of the Church," he continued.

Army regulations permit soldiers to seek religious exemptions or accommodations.

It is unclear how the military intends to select members for the firing squad.

"The U.S. military generally enjoys a good reputation in the world," Broglio said. "Is there really a value to throwing them in the same boat with terrorists by broadcasting the image of the execution of a man in a wheelchair to the whole world?"

A U.S. government execution has never been broadcast to the public, making it an unprecedented plan that has drawn backlash from political and religious leaders.

Broglio joins other Catholic leaders in criticizing the Pentagon's plans to livestream the execution.

Major Nidal Malik Hasan is set to be executed at Fort Hood on Dec. 3, which would make him the first person to be executed by firing squad by the U.S. military since 1945. (REUTERS/Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences/Handout)

The head of the U.S. bishops conference, Archbishop Paul Coakley, expressed "shock" and "great sorrow" about the public execution plan and urged the U.S. to reconsider.

"In no way can Hasan’s actions be condoned but this decision is a barbaric promotion of a culture of death and must be reconsidered," he said in a statement on Friday. "The public execution even of one who has done grave harm will only further undermine the moral fabric of our nation and be a blight on the conscience of its people."

Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican secretary of state, called the proposed broadcast "truly incomprehensible" and warned that it was "unacceptable to turn death into a spectacle."

"The Church’s position is one of total opposition to the death penalty; it is incompatible with human dignity and serves as no deterrent," Parolin told reporters on Friday.

According to the English translation published by Vatican News, Parolin said, "It is truly incomprehensible that anyone would want to use this method in this day and age. I do not know for what purpose. It is certainly unacceptable to turn death into a spectacle. However guilty the person may be, there are other ways."

Parolin added that the death penalty "is incompatible with human dignity and does not serve as a deterrent."

Pope Leo XIV reiterated the Catholic Church's opposition to the death penalty as "inadmissible" in a social media post on Saturday marking World Day Against the Death Penalty.

Citing Catholic doctrine revised under his predecessor, Pope Francis, Leo emphasized that the death penalty violates human dignity.

"The death penalty is inadmissible because it is an attack on the inviolability and dignity of the person. The common good can be safeguarded and the requirements of justice can be met without recourse to capital punishment: effective systems of detention have been developed that protect citizens while at the same time do not completely deprive those who are guilty of the possibility of redemption," Leo, the first American pope, wrote on X without specifically mentioning the Pentagon's execution plan for Hasan.

FORT HOOD SHOOTER SHOULD BE EXECUTED '13 TIMES OVER' — BUT NOT ON LIVE STREAM, SURVIVOR SAYS

A U.S. government execution has never been broadcast to the general public, making it an unprecedented plan that has drawn backlash from political and religious leaders. (Aaron Schwartz / AFP via Getty Images)

President Donald Trump said Saturday he had not yet decided whether to allow the livestream plan to move forward, although he has reportedly expressed doubts in private about broadcasting the execution.

Vice President JD Vance, who is a Catholic, expressed skepticism about whether the Pentagon would proceed with a public execution. He said he would not watch the livestream if it were carried out.

Several lawmakers, including Republicans, have spoken out against plans to broadcast the execution.

"Public executions are what oppressive dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan do," Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., said on Thursday. "It should not be happening in America."

articles.title: Emir says Qatar has shown resilience in the face of ‘exceptional events’
articles.excerpt:
Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani has told the Shura Council that the region has faced “exceptional events”, during months of instability amid the United States-Israeli war on Iran.

Speaki...
articles.body_text:
Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani has told the Shura Council that the region has faced “exceptional events”, during months of instability amid the United States-Israeli war on Iran.

Speaking in the capital, Doha, on Tuesday, Sheikh Tamim said Qatar’s response had shown its resilience.

“Our country and the region have faced exceptional events that have once again proven the cohesion of state institutions,” the Emir said.

Qatar has found itself caught up in the war, which began on February 28 and has triggered a global energy crisis.

The Gulf state has been directly attacked by Iran on several occasions, including in March, when Tehran struck Qatar’s Ras Laffan gas facility, the world’s largest liquefied natural gas (LNG) production site.

Sheikh Tamim said Qatar had been able to absorb the consequences of the regional instability due to policies implemented before the war, stressing that Doha’s preference was to resolve conflicts through peaceful means and dialogue. However, the Emir maintained that the Gulf Cooperation Council’s (GCC) security was non-negotiable.

“The security of Gulf Cooperation Council states and the preservation of their sovereignty are matters that cannot be compromised on,” he said.

The war on Iran has disrupted global supply routes, particularly the Strait of Hormuz, which Tehran has effectively blocked since the start of the conflict.

Sheikh Tamim said efforts to safeguard maritime routes must be increased.

“Efforts must be doubled to secure navigation in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz and to protect energy facilities and civilian infrastructure,” he said.

Reporting from Doha, Al Jazeera’s Zein Basravi said Sheikh Tamim had used the address to reiterate Qatar’s preference for ending wars and resolving disagreements through peaceful dialogue, while reaffirming the country’s commitment to the Palestinian cause.

“He highlighted how the attacks on LNG facilities have effectively hurt Qatar’s capacity, it has hurt Qatar’s economy directly,” Basravi said.

“He also cautioned and said that ‘we should not be like we were before this crisis going forward’. Certainly, a signal that will be taken seriously by those in this chamber; by people heading up institutions.”

“If you read between the lines, the signal is clear, that they will lean into non-carbon related industries.”

Sheikh Tamim said Qatar has invested more than $60bn across a variety of areas, including infrastructure projects, public-private partnerships and private sector investment.

Rashid Al-Mohanadi, vice president of the Center for International Policy Research, told Al Jazeera that Qatar has a history of “turning crises into opportunities”.

“In the last 10 years, Qatar has been through many challenges and usually the output is we become more resilient. The hope is that after this war, which has been very challenging on the population [and] on the economy, that Qatar will turn out stronger and more resilient,” Al-Mohanadi said.

articles.title: Malaysia’s Firefly cancels flights to Singapore over haze from Indonesia
articles.excerpt: Firefly, a Malaysian low-cost airline, has extended the suspension of its flights between Kuala Lumpur and Singapore through Wednesday as smoke from fires in Indonesia continued to blanket the region....
articles.body_text:
Firefly, a Malaysian low-cost airline, has extended the suspension of its flights between Kuala Lumpur and Singapore through Wednesday as smoke from fires in Indonesia continued to blanket the region.

The announcement came as IQAir, an air quality monitor, ranked Singapore and the Malaysian capital Kuala Lumpur as the world’s two most polluted cities on Tuesday.

Firefly said in a statement that flights between the Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport (SZB) near Kuala Lumpur and the Seletar Airport in Singapore (XSP) have been cancelled up to Wednesday due to “weather and haze conditions”.

It called the action a “proactive safety measure”.

The fires, mostly on the Indonesian islands of Sumatra and Borneo, are the country’s most intense in 11 years. They have been spurred by El Nino, a weather pattern expected to be among the strongest in four decades.

IQAir, a Swiss air quality monitoring company, said Air Quality Index in Singapore stood at 199 on Tuesday and 183 in Kuala Lumpur. Readings above 150 are generally considered unhealthy, and those above 300 are classified as hazardous.

Firefly, a subsidiary of Malaysia Aviation Group, which includes Malaysia Airlines, first announced the flight cancellations on October 10, citing “low visibility” due to the haze conditions.

Firefly said that affected passengers were being rebooked on Malaysia Airlines flights between Kuala Lumpur International Airport and Singapore’s Changi Airport, subject to seat availability.

The Singapore government has reintroduced subsidised care for haze-related illnesses, as it last did in 2015, when smoke from Indonesian fires hung over the region for weeks.

In Malaysia, schools reopened in most states on Tuesday as air quality improved slightly, but they remain closed in three states, one federal territory and several districts.

Malaysia’s foreign minister, Mohamad Hasan, said on Monday that he would press for stronger regional mechanisms when foreign ministers of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) meet next month.

“We already have an ASEAN mechanism for natural disasters, but haze is not included or classified as a natural disaster,” he told reporters in Sepang, according to Bernama, Malaysia’s state news agency.

The Philippines, which chairs the bloc this year, confirmed that the issue would be on the agenda.

“It’s in the agenda,” Dominic Xavier Imperial, a spokesman for the Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs, said of the November meeting, which will precede the 49th ASEAN summit in Manila.

Mohamad, the Malaysian minister, said Indonesia had deployed about 60,000 personnel to fight the fires, but thick smoke had grounded 34 aircraft, including planes and helicopters.

Remote terrain and limited water supplies have also hindered the effort, he said, and cloud seeding is not possible without suitable rain clouds. He acknowledged Indonesia’s efforts but urged more effective action, citing the toll on Malaysian communities.

articles.title: Imran Khan’s PTI braces to fight federal takeover of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
articles.excerpt: Islamabad, Pakistan – The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party of jailed ex-Prime Minister Imran Khan is planning to legally challenge the federal government’s Sunday takeover of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, a...
articles.body_text:
Islamabad, Pakistan – The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party of jailed ex-Prime Minister Imran Khan is planning to legally challenge the federal government’s Sunday takeover of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, a province that the party governed.

Sheikh Waqas Akram, the PTI’s central information secretary, told Al Jazeera that the party would challenge the imposition of emergency laws – suspending civil liberties – and governor’s rule in the province in court on Tuesday. A petition had been drafted by a legal committee headed by PTI Secretary-General Salman Akram Raja, but Akram did not say whether it would be filed in the Supreme Court or the Federal Constitutional Court.

The federal government’s moves have emerged as Pakistan’s latest political flashpoint, with competing narratives from the government and the PTI, at a time when the party was in the middle of a delayed march towards Islamabad, aimed at pressuring authorities to release former PM Khan, who has been jailed for more than three years.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Monday justified the government’s moves by arguing that federal rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa was needed for Pakistan to effectively combat “terrorism” in the province that shares a porous border with Afghanistan.

“No war can be won, however many resources you bring, whatever you do, until the government there leads it,” Naqvi said in Peshawar on Monday.

On Sunday, President Asif Ali Zardari imposed emergency rule and governor’s rule, suspending the PTI government in the northwestern province. The party has governed Khyber Pakhtunkhwa since 2013.

Sohail Afridi, the suspended chief minister, and some members of his cabinet have been taken into preventive custody, Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry confirmed on Monday. Afridi had been leading the march towards Islamabad seeking to free Khan, and despite the setbacks to the party, PTI leaders said the protest was still on.

“The long march has not ended. But a historic crackdown against the party has begun,” Akram said.

According to the proclamation signed on Sunday, the provincial government had “failed to demonstrate the ownership, will and intent to adequately deal with the menace of terrorism”.

“The federal government’s position is clearly described. ‘A deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism’ as communicated after cabinet meeting. That’s the constitutional premise needed for imposition of emergency,” Aasiya Riaz, joint director of the independent political think tank the Pakistan Institute of Legislative Development and Transparency (PILDAT), told Al Jazeera.

However, Hassan Abdullah Niazi, an adjunct faculty member at the Lahore University of Management Sciences (LUMS) and a lawyer based in Lahore, disputed that premise.

“If all of this was true, then KP would be in a state of anarchy, but we know that is not the case. It had a functioning legislature and executive that commanded the confidence of the people, hence this entire exercise is an unconstitutional move against provincial autonomy,” he told Al Jazeera.

A more detailed case was set out last month in a 14-page white paper presented in Islamabad by Ikhtiar Wali Khan, a political adviser to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif from the ruling Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PMLN).

The paper pointed to rising police deaths, staff and equipment shortages in the provincial counterterrorism department, and spending priorities.

However, Akram rejected the charge that the PTI had failed to lead the fight.

He said the provincial government had paid 1.83 billion rupees ($6.6m) from its own funds to the families of more than 900 soldiers, police and paramilitary personnel killed fighting armed groups, a contribution he said no other province had made.

Naqvi said at a news conference in Islamabad on Sunday that the federal government had been involved in negotiations with the PTI on a proposed “sit-in” by the party in support of Khan.

“We have no problem with the sit-in. Do the sit-in as eagerly as you like; we have no issue with the sit-in. Our issue is entirely terrorism-related, and we want to get you on board on that,” he said.

Taimur Jhagra, a PTI leader and former provincial finance and health minister, said the talks with the government that the party had agreed to were meant to focus on Khan.

“It’s absurd that a negotiation about a protest movement to give Imran Khan Supreme Court-ordered medical and visitation rights becomes a negotiation about terrorism strategy,” he told Al Jazeera.

Naqvi also said the PTI had agreed during the talks that emergency rule should be imposed in 12 districts of the province.

Akram rejected that claim and said the party had refused. The party feared residents would bear the cost of military operations, he said.

“We said ‘No, this cannot be. You cannot do whatever you like with them. We took the votes from them. Tomorrow they will blame us: ‘You got us killed,’” he said.

Akram said the PTI negotiators referred the federal government’s proposal to Afridi, who rejected it.

Federal Information Minister Attaullah Tarar went further at Sunday’s news conference.

“This government, which has been suspended through a constitutional option, is responsible for the deaths of thousands of citizens of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa,” he said, accusing Afridi’s PTI government of being hand in glove with the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan – an armed group known as the Pakistan Taliban – and the Afghan Taliban.

There is no known or public evidence of any such links.

According to a government white paper, 122 police personnel were killed in the province in the first half of this year, up from 63 during the same period in 2025.

Independent trackers also point to rising violence. The Centre for Research and Security Studies (CRSS), an Islamabad-based think tank, recorded 556 violence-linked deaths in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa between July and September, up from 475 in the previous quarter and 311 in the one before.

Balochistan was hit harder. Deaths there rose by 213 percent to 829, making it the worst-affected province, according to CRSS.

The government says it acted because the provincial administration would not lead the fight against armed groups, but analysts disagree over the takeover’s purpose.

“I would say this decision is political, administrative and security. All three elements are present in it,” Zaigham Khan, an Islamabad-based political analyst, told Al Jazeera.

Ali Arqam, a longtime observer of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, disagreed.

“This is not really about security at all. It is basically a political move that they are just dressing up as some kind of administrative necessity,” he told Al Jazeera.

Jhagra said the government believed the takeover would break the PTI, but argued that people across the country still saw Khan as their leader.

“It is trying to solve for legitimacy,” he told Al Jazeera, referring to the government.

For his part, Federal Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar said at a news conference in Islamabad on Sunday that the decision was a purely constitutional step.

For the PTI, the immediate concerns are its leaders and the courts.

“There has been no contact. No one in the party has had any contact with the chief minister,” Akram said.

But the party remains widely popular, in the province and nationally.

At Monday’s meeting, Naqvi said results against “terrorism” would not come in a day. There would be ups and downs, he said, and harder times lay ahead.

But Arqam, the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa observer, said Islamabad should be judged by the same measures as the PTI government.

“You test this government by looking at the exact same hard metrics: Does security actually improve, do the basic services get better, and do the promised fiscal resources finally show up?” he said.

articles.title: Australian politics live: businesses increasing prices under cover of surcharge ban, UBS economists warn; fire ants in Sydney’s inner west
articles.excerpt:
Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Retailers are using the credit card surcharge ban to justify larger price increases, according to UBS economists.

Businesses were banned f...
articles.body_text:
Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Retailers are using the credit card surcharge ban to justify larger price increases, according to UBS economists.

Businesses were banned from including transaction surcharges from 1 October as part of a Reserve Bank-led reforms aimed at improving transparency for customers and, ultimately, lowering bank fees.

The RBA has predicted that shops would incorporate the bank fees into the final sale price, likely leading to a 0.1 percentage point increase to inflation.

But the UBS economists in a note to clients said this estimate was too low and that there was evidence that businesses, such as cafes, were using the surcharge ban as cover to pass on bigger price rises.

“The RBA’s estimate seems a lower bound estimate, particularly given recent increases in fuel and other input costs,” they said, estimating a 0.2% boost to inflation.

According to a survey of more than 1,500 cafes by Small Flat White, an online coffee price tracker, 17% of cafes have increased their prices since the start of the surcharge ban, with an average increase of 50 cents, or more than 10%.

That is multiples of the typical 1.5% card surcharge fee. The UBS economists said:

double quotation markResilient demand and still-elevated inflation expectations may be allowing merchants to use the change as ‘cover’ to pass through broader cost pressures (wages, fuel, and other input costs).

Following years of above-target inflation, consumers may be more accepting of price rises. Evidence of ‘round up’ pricing in items such as coffee suggests pass-through could exceed the surcharge itself.

Digital duty of care may be delayed by Senate inquiry

The Greens are considering seeking to refer Labor’s digital duty of care legislation to a Senate inquiry, potentially delaying the bill which is expected to be introduced this week.

Communications minister Anika Wells is at the National Press Club on Thursday to discuss the legislation. But with the Coalition again dealing itself out of negotiations and refusing to consider it, the Greens are in the box seat for this legislation, and the minor party may want to see it pushed to an inquiry.

The Greens will seek “improvements” to the bill, but say they are not interested in “killing” the proposal. The parliament’s sitting calendar only has two Senate weeks between now and the end of the year, with Senate estimates at the end of October, so the Greens say they want to look at the bill now, ahead of the usual end-of-year chaos.

We’ll keep you updated as that progresses.

You can also read more about the legislation, and the disagreement between Labor and the Greens in relation to the proposed laws, here:

Coalition senator Jonathon Duniam rejects claims PM’s office meddled with AI letter

The outgoing shadow home affairs minister, Jonathon Duniam, has been interviewed on Sky News about his role on a parliamentary committee considering AI policy.

We brought you the news earlier today that a senior adviser in Anthony Albanese’s office had made edits and comments in a bipartisan letter from the committee before it was sent to the prime minister, a move which committee member David Pocock said was concerning.

Pocock said he was concerned at the intervention of Albanese’s team in the letter, which raises concerns about copyright, AI safeguards, sovereign capability and AI literacy.

Duniam, who was the deputy chair of the committee, sent the letter with the Labor MP and inquiry chair, Jo Briskey, last night, on behalf of Labor, Coalition and crossbench MPs.

Duniam had already said there was “no guidance, no interference” with the committee’s work and he would be “the first person out of the blocks to criticise the government if the prime minister wasn’t showing interest in the committee’s work”.

He rejected Pocock’s assertions again during his interview on Sky a short time ago, saying that:

double quotation markWell, I’d love to know what’s not in the letter that should be included that’s been missed out.

I saw some comments that the letter had been heavily vetted, I’m not sure what’s been deleted.
  I think it is good that decision making entities like the PMO have been actively interested in what we do… That does not remove the independence of the committee.

The committee does not do what either Anthony Albanese or Angus Taylor says, the committee does what it determines is the right way to go.

And to be clear, the parliament will be master of its own destiny when it comes to things like copyright legislation.

The shadow home affairs minister, Jonathon Duniam, is expected to give his valedictory speech this week and leave parliament at the end of October.

The frontbencher announced he would be resigning from the Senate back in June but committed to stay until the end of the year.

Duniam is expected to stay for the final sitting week of October, which will include Senate estimates. He was first elected as a Liberal senator representing Tasmania in 2016.

It means the Liberal leader, Angus Taylor, will have another frontbench position to fill – which could see a minor shadow cabinet reshuffle.

Retailers are using the credit card surcharge ban to justify larger price increases, according to UBS economists.

Businesses were banned from including transaction surcharges from 1 October as part of a Reserve Bank-led reforms aimed at improving transparency for customers and, ultimately, lowering bank fees.

The RBA has predicted that shops would incorporate the bank fees into the final sale price, likely leading to a 0.1 percentage point increase to inflation.

But the UBS economists in a note to clients said this estimate was too low and that there was evidence that businesses, such as cafes, were using the surcharge ban as cover to pass on bigger price rises.

“The RBA’s estimate seems a lower bound estimate, particularly given recent increases in fuel and other input costs,” they said, estimating a 0.2% boost to inflation.

According to a survey of more than 1,500 cafes by Small Flat White, an online coffee price tracker, 17% of cafes have increased their prices since the start of the surcharge ban, with an average increase of 50 cents, or more than 10%.

That is multiples of the typical 1.5% card surcharge fee. The UBS economists said:

double quotation markResilient demand and still-elevated inflation expectations may be allowing merchants to use the change as ‘cover’ to pass through broader cost pressures (wages, fuel, and other input costs).

Following years of above-target inflation, consumers may be more accepting of price rises. Evidence of ‘round up’ pricing in items such as coffee suggests pass-through could exceed the surcharge itself.

Labor, Greens and Coalition party rooms finish up their meetings before parliament sits

The party rooms are finishing up their meetings that happen every Tuesday during sitting weeks.

They are a chance for the party leaders to give their caucus a bit of a gee-up and discuss their position on upcoming pieces of legislation.

That happens before the parliament sitting at midday today.

This morning, Angus Taylor let cameras in to cover his preamble, declaring “project Albanese has failed”.

double quotation markWe have seen Australia going backwards in the wrong direction like at no time in my lifetime. We have a responsibility to deliver that plan that I just talked about, to fix our economy, to protect our way of life.

Real estate can be tight in Parliament House.

So much so that a couple of cabinet ministers were left waiting patiently on the sidelines to have their turn to address the media.

The mural hall, a popular spot for a press conference, has been in hot demand this morning.

US livestreaming Fort Hood firing squad execution ‘repugnant’, Liberal Ted O’Brien says

The shadow foreign affairs minister, Ted O’Brien, says his party has written to the eSafety commissioner to see what can be done to stop the live stream of an execution in the US planned for December. The eSafety commissioner said overnight her office did not have the powers to proactively prevent the stream being shown in Australia.

Speaking to News24, O’Brien says he’s concerned children in Australia are already talking about the execution.

double quotation markYou can respect the sovereignty of the United States, while also speaking personally, and saying that I find the idea of livestreaming capital punishment repugnant. It’s not anything I want to see in Australia.

I’ve heard stories of schoolkids now in Australia talking about this, talking about watching this on their screens, on their devices. That is not the Australia that I want. Candidly, I don’t think it’s the Australia any of us really want … That’s not, that doesn’t align to our values at all.

Fire ants detected at logistics centre in Sydney’s inner west

The New South Wales government says it is responding to the detection of a red fire ant nest at the a logistics centre in Sydney’s inner west.

Federal biosecurity officers discovered the ants in a lure used to detect and monitor invasive species. A nest was then found and treated, with genetic analysis confirming the ants likely arrived from overseas via a container.

The state government said specialist fire ant detection dog teams had undertaken surveillance at the Enfield Intermodal Logistics Centre and in the immediate vicinity and no other nests had been found at the site.

Fire ants are one of the world’s worst invasive species. They can sting people and livestock and cause serious harm to the environment and local economies.

The NSW agriculture minister, Tara Moriarty, said:

double quotation markIt’s important to note that no further ants have been found, but we are focused on making sure any potential spread is identified and eradicated quickly.

While fire ants are one of the world’s most invasive species, they can and have been successfully eradicated in New South Wales.

She said the government would work with the local inner west community over the next two weeks “to build awareness, educate and assist members of the public with monitoring for fire ants to contain this invasive pest”.

She said the immediate focus was on inspecting and, if necessary, treating properties within a 500m radius of the centre, followed by surveillance of properties within a 2km radius.

Emergency crews sent to restore power after Alice Springs storms

The Northern Territory chief minister, Lia Finocchiaro, has sent extra emergency crews from Darwin to help restore power after Alice Springs was battered by a destructive storm.

This article includes content provided by Instagram. We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content, click 'Allow and continue'.

Thousands of homes lost power in Alice Springs on Monday when the storm toppled trees and power lines, pelted the town with large hailstones and caused widespread damage. In a statement Finocchiaro said:

double quotation markOur thoughts are with the many Alice Springs residents who have been affected by this destructive storm. We are here to help you get back on your feet as soon as possible

The State Emergency Service responded to more than 100 calls for help. The NT government said no injuries had been reported.

All events on Monday night’s program for the Alice Springs Masters Games were called off after the storm tore through but organisers were confident delayed events could be rescheduled.

David Pocock says a letter written by the parliamentary AI committee sent to the prime minister on Monday night was “heavily vetted” by his office.

The letter with edits and suggestions from a senior adviser in the prime minister’s office, seen by Guardian Australia, shows the adviser made multiple suggestions and wrote “fine” on some content.

Pocock tells News24 he’s concerned the committee is being used to get a predetermined outcome for the government.

double quotation markOne of the other things that I’m really concerned about is that when I actually loaded the letter up on to my computer, there’s a whole bunch of track changes from the PM’s office. So this is meant to be a letter from the committee, but clearly has been heavily vetted by the prime minister’s office.

I’m concerned that the major parties are working together to potentially get a preconceived outcome rather than actually listening to experts, listening to the community and saying, hey, this is a massive challenge we’re facing.

Pocock says he raised concerns with the chair of the committee.

But he does say there are good recommendations in the letter and that it calls for safeguards that the government shelved a couple of years ago.

‘100% of nothing’: AI committee recommends stronger copyright laws

The parliamentary AI committee has recommended stronger copyright protections to ensure creatives have control over how their works are used.

Labor MP and committee chair Jo Briskey and deputy chair, Liberal frontbencher Jonno Duniam are holding a press conference in parliament after the committee wrote a letter to the prime minister making several recommendations.

double quotation markAt the moment, you’ve got a situation where data, copyright, intellectual property, whatever form it comes in, is currently being used by offshore models. It’s being harvested to train models offshore. And do you know how much our copyrights holders are getting as a result? 100% of nothing.

The letter to the prime minister says the government should examine current copyright settings and “prioritise ensuring that Australian creators retain control over how their works are used, that they are paid, and that AI systems reflect Australian values and culture.”

But David Pocock – a crossbench committee member – says the recommendations don’t go far enough to protect creatives. He told News24 in a separate interview:

double quotation markI think the committee has done some good work so far. I’ve raised concerns last night about some of the lack of detail around things like copyright and artists and journalists wanting to maintain the current way that our copyright laws work and actually forcing these big frontier labs to do deals.

During a more tense moment on News24 this morning, Coalition frontbencher Jonno Duniam says Labor is trying to use Josh Frydenberg to deflect from their own problems.

The government has been under pressure over the ATO’s decision to ban credit card payments from November, as well as a series of increasingly difficult economic moves, including interest rates at a 15-year high.

Labor frontbencher Daniel Mulino said the Coalition had “a leader in waiting outside of parliament saying we need to jack up the GST”.

That’s a reference to Frydenberg’s new book, released today, and his pitch for an increase to the GST.

Duniam called the comments “a masterclass in deflection”.

“I just have had the insight into the Labor talking points for today,” Duniam said. “If it starts getting tough, start talking about Josh Frydenberg.”

double quotation markI mean, seriously, they say they know Australians are doing it tougher, in business or just a household trying to pay the bills.

They’re doing nothing about it, except making political points around what’s happening here in Canberra.

Greens senator Sarah Hanson-Young says she doesn’t think she’ll run for the party leadership again, after putting her hand up when Larissa Waters stepped down at the end of September.

Hanson-Young was in a three way contest with Mehreen Faruqi and David Shoebridge – the latter of whom won.

The senator from South Australia will mark 20 years in parliament next year.

double quotation markI don’t think so ... I put my hat in the ring, of course, a couple of weeks ago when the position was vacant. I put forward a vision for a positive, optimistic, and a caring and defiant progressive force.

She says Shoebridge has “done a good job hitting the road very quickly” and that the party is spreading a positive message.

Greens still in negotiations over digital duty of care bill

The Greens still want bigger fines and the ability for individuals to sue tech platforms as they negotiate over Labor’s digital duty of care bill.

The Coalition have pretty much ruled themselves out of negotiations, saying publicly the bill should be scrapped entirely and started over.

Sarah Hanson-Young tells RN Breakfast she was pleased the government is removing ministerial discretion powers under the legislation, but she wants more before she’s willing to give the bill support.

double quotation markThe proposed fines from the government are around $99m, $100m, that’s peanuts to these big global companies … All the experts around the world say that if you want to hit big tech where it hurts, if you want to hold them accountable and make them pay for the consequences of their harm and damage, that it needs to be a percentage of global revenue.

Two is making sure that Australians and community groups can also take action against these big tech platforms because otherwise it’s just left to the eSafety commissioner, the regulator. And individual Australians, individual users, should be able to complain and have compensation if they are indeed harmed online.

Greens senator Sarah Hanson-Young says the prime minister needs to call president Trump to express Australia’s dismay over the planned livestreamed execution by firing squad.

She says the government should also “jump on the phone” with the big tech companies to stop them allowing the stream on their platforms.

The eSafety commissioner revealed overnight she did not have the powers to proactively prevent the stream from being shown or accessed in Australia.

She adds, if the laws need to be fixed to prevent the live stream – or any future live stream – that should be done.

double quotation markThe Australian government needs to pick up the phone to the United States president and to the US administration. I mean, this is barbaric … the idea that a state-sanctioned killing would be televised, would be livestreamed as content, almost for entertainment value, as a government PR episode. I mean, it is revolting, it is barbaric, and it must be called out.

And Australians should be protected from it. If the law needs to be fixed, the government should get on and fix it.

articles.title: ABC accuses FCC of trying to 'inflict maximal coercive pressure' with probe against network
articles.excerpt:
FCC Chairman Brendan Carr spoke with Fox News Digital on what he calls the "meritless" lawsuit brought by ABC and Disney.

Disney and ABC accused the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on Monday ...
articles.body_text:
FCC Chairman Brendan Carr spoke with Fox News Digital on what he calls the "meritless" lawsuit brought by ABC and Disney.

Disney and ABC accused the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on Monday of using the license renewal process to circumvent "judicial review" and inflict "maximal coercive pressure" against the network and company.

Disney originally sued the FCC in August over what it claimed was a "retaliatory campaign against ABC" regarding the agency's early broadcast license renewal proceedings for eight ABC-owned stations earlier this year. The stations, according to the FCC, must demonstrate they are operating in the public interest as the agency investigates diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) practices.

However, in Disney's latest filing, the company asserted that the FCC could have used "a number of different tools" to investigate Disney and ABC's DEI practices that did not involve forcing stations to renew their licenses years ahead of schedule, suggesting it was done to avoid legal scrutiny.

ABC MORE CAUTIOUS OF BOOKING CANDIDATES ON 'THE VIEW' AMID FCC PRESSURE, DISNEY'S FIRST AMENDMENT LAWSUIT SAYS

ABC and Disney filed another scathing response against the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) on Monday. (Gary Hershorn/Getty Images)

"These are not merely 'theoretical' tools ... they have been used by the agency for decades," the filing read. "Yet the agency tried none of those less intrusive tools here, instead taking the unprecedented step of calling for early license renewal of all eight ABC-owned stations at once. Defendants’ own admissions leave no doubt as to why — Defendants sought to inflict maximal coercive pressure on the media company whose speech the Administration sought to curb, while deliberately evading judicial review."

Disney cited a court hearing last week in which the FCC was instructed to provide a supplemental filing on alternative methods the agency could have used. During the hearing, the FCC suggested that additional procedures would have required federal court enforcement.

"That Defendants openly describe judicial review as an obstacle demonstrates what Plaintiffs have been saying all along: shielding their unconstitutional campaign against ABC from judicial review is part of Defendants’ retaliatory strategy," the filing read.

In a comment to Fox News Digital, FCC spokesperson Adam Jackman dismissed the latest filing as an effort to block the FCC in court procedures.

CONSERVATIVE GROUPS URGE FCC TO BACK OFF ABC LICENSE REVIEW, WARNING IT COULD HURT RIGHT-LEANING MEDIA

ABC and Disney accused the FCC of launching a retaliation campaign against the company on behalf of the Trump administration. (Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images)

"Disney’s latest filing only confirms that they’ve filed a meritless case in the wrong court at the wrong time," Jackman said. "They want a district court to prevent the FCC from even considering whether Disney has complied with its longstanding obligations as a broadcaster. The law does not allow that. The FCC will continue to hold broadcasters accountable to their regulatory obligations."

Fox News Digital also reached out to ABC and Disney for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

Disney and ABC have repeatedly attacked the FCC's probes and investigations into the company as a form of retaliation over programs and hosts that are critical of President Donald Trump, such as late-night host Jimmy Kimmel.

DISNEY ACCUSES TRUMP'S FCC OF ATTEMPTING TO 'SUPPRESS SPEECH' WITH LICENSE RENEWAL INVESTIGATION

The FCC also launched a probe into ABC's daytime talk show "The View." (Lou Rocco/Getty Images)

In addition to the license renewal proceedings, the FCC has launched a probe into the ABC daytime talk show "The View" based on the agency's demand that broadcast stations adhere to the equal opportunity requirement stating opposing political candidates receive equal time. Disney has maintained that "The View" is a "bona fide news" program exempted from the rule.

Lindsay Kornick is an associate editor for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to lindsay.kornick@fox.com and on Twitter: @lmkornick.

articles.title: Dodgers dynasty on the brink after the Milwaukee BABIP machine dials up another win for Brewers
articles.excerpt:
Aaron Ashby joins John Smoltz on King of the Diamond to discuss the Milwaukee Brewers’ Game 1 win over the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Game 2 of the National League Championship Series on Monday afternoon w...
articles.body_text:
Aaron Ashby joins John Smoltz on King of the Diamond to discuss the Milwaukee Brewers’ Game 1 win over the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Game 2 of the National League Championship Series on Monday afternoon was a must-win for the Los Angeles Dodgers.

Despite widespread perception that the Dodgers are the unbeatable superteam, it was Milwaukee, the team that finished with the best record in the league, that played essentially flawless baseball in a Game 1 win. While Jacob Misiorowski wasn't his typically dominant self, every time Los Angeles had an opportunity to break the game open, "The Miz" and his team's defense clamped down.

Already up a run in the second inning, the Dodgers had the bases loaded with postseason star Kike Hernandez at the plate. Once again, the Brewers defense was perfectly positioned to turn the inning-ending double play. After Milwaukee's offense scratched across two runs against Tarik Skubal, their bullpen continued its remarkable run of success, going 4.2 scoreless innings to secure the win.

BRIGHT LIGHTS NOT TOO BRIGHT FOR THE BREWERS OR SUPERFAN FRONT ROW AMY IN GAME 1 OF NLCS

Still, the Dodgers felt good about their chances with Yoshinobu Yamamoto, postseason hero from 2025, starting in Game 2 against Logan Henderson. Yet for all the hype about LA's remarkable rotation, the Milwaukee BABIP (batting average on balls in play) machine once again kicked into high gear to secure a massive 2-0 series lead and put the Dodgers' three-peat hopes on life support with a 7-4 win.

LA jumped out to an early lead thanks to some uncharacteristic sloppiness from the Brewers. Mookie Betts walked, Freddie Freeman moved him to second, and he took third on a wild pitch from starter Logan Henderson. Teoscar Hernandez knocked him in with a sacrifice fly, and the Dodgers had a 1-0 lead without a hit. Sure enough though, Milwaukee immediately tied it in the bottom of the first.

The Dodgers missed an opportunity to challenge an obvious missed strike three call on Brice Turang, who then doubled and scored on a patented Brewers bloop single. William Contreras stuck his bat out with one hand, somehow making contact with Yamamoto's pitch to dump it into left field. It wouldn't be the last time.

Milwaukee Brewers catcher William Contreras celebrates his home run during the fifth inning of Game 2 of the National League Championship Series between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Los Angeles Dodgers on Monday, Oct. 12, 2026, in Milwaukee. (AP Photo/Abbie Parr)

The third inning was a near-repeat. LA mounted a quick rally on back-to-back singles from Tommy Edman and Mookie Betts. Sal Frelick robbed Freddie Freeman of a double with a nice running catch in the right center field gap, but an error on a pickoff attempt at first base brought Edman in to score. But the Brewers, knowing that the Dodgers' greatest weakness is having an opportunity to score runs, had them right where they wanted them. Easy outs from Teoscar Hernandez and Shohei Ohtani ended the "threat," and Milwaukee answered right back in the bottom of the inning.

David Hamilton poked another bloop single, stole second, and yet again, Brice Turang reached base on a missed strike three that went unchallenged by catcher Will Smith. Jake Bauers, one of the worst hitters in baseball before putting on a Milwaukee uniform, worked a walk after a lengthy at bat against Yamamoto, and Christian Yelich made him pay for it with a single to center.

After all this playoff heroics in 2025, Yamamoto went just 2.2 innings, allowing four hits and three runs. Missed challenges, bloop singles, exceptionally well-timed line drives from below average hitters, the ideal Milwaukee offensive outing.

Now trailing 3-2, the Dodgers "fought" back in the fifth. Kyle Tucker led off with a double, before a throwing error from Henderson on a Tommy Edman bunt let him score and sent Edman to second. A grounder and sac fly gave LA a 4-3 lead, once again without getting a hit with runners in scoring position.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Milwaukee Brewers designated hitter Christian Yelich runs after hitting a two-RBI base hit during the third inning of Game 2 of the National League Championship Series against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Monday, Oct. 12, 2026, in Milwaukee. (AP Photo/Ashley Landis)

Sure enough, William Contreras immediately tied it in the bottom of the inning with a mammoth homer to left-center.

The Brewers bullpen, which is apparently unhittable, put up another scoreless inning, before the Milwaukee superteam once again kicked into high gear in the bottom of the sixth. Hamilton reached on a hit by pitch, advanced to second after a poor pickoff attempt, went to third on a Jackson Chourio grounder, and scored on yet another end of the bat blooper from Contreras.

Again, the Brewers' relief pitchers proved to be the single greatest pitching unit ever assembled, extending their streak to nearly 29 innings with just one run allowed. Monday was the first time in playoff history that a team's bullpen went over five innings in a postseason game without giving up a baserunner. JoJo Romero, Abner Uribe, Trevor Megill, Aaron Ashby, DL Hall...that's the real superteam, and it cost about $17 to build it.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The BABIP continued into the eighth, as David Hamilton crushed a 73mph single to right field, stole second, and scored on yet another obliterated 71mph single from Brice Turang. That hit pushed the Brewers to 5-12 with RISP.

Jake Bauers added on with yet another 73mph bloop single to make Milwaukee 6-13 with RISP.

Somehow, Milwaukee has perfected the art of running into singles on poorly hit balls in play. Some might say it's a skill, but decades of data and information have told us it isn't. Players and teams with poor exit velocities don't outperform with batting average on balls in play, in fact, it's the opposite.

The league leaders in hard hit percentage this season were, in order:

All five had BABIPs at or above league average, Wood and De La Cruz were .344 and .359, respectively. Jac Caglianone was eighth in hard hit percentage and second in baseball in BABIP. Hitting the ball hard is a skill, soft contact isn't. Yet the Brewers have three hitters in the top seven in BABIP anyway.

Milwaukee Brewers second baseman Brice Turang celebrates his RBI base hit during the eighth inning of Game 2 of the National League Championship Series against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Monday, Oct. 12, 2026, in Milwaukee. (AP Photo/Ashley Landis)

Does it matter that Milwaukee has likely been lucky this season? No, not at all. A playoff series is the epitome of a small sample size, and reversion to the mean doesn't have to happen over five-to-seven games. Contreras could hit 17 straight bloopers off the end of the bat, because that's baseball. Which is why predictions of a guaranteed Dodgers' World Series win because of their talent were always so laughable.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

Milwaukee had more hits with runners in scoring position in this game, not one hit hard, than the Dodgers have all postseason. And they're going back to LA with a 2-0 series lead and overwhelming likelihood of advancing to the World Series. The gaps between teams in baseball are so small that a bounce here or there, a team's ability to magically ensure that 71mph bloopers are placed perfectly, despite there being no ability to do that, can change a playoff series. David Hamilton, who is objectively an awful baseball player, reached base four times and scored two runs. Shohei Ohtani, the best player in the history of baseball, was useless. That's not unusual or unexpected, it's part of the sport. Which is why it's impossible for one team to guarantee themselves anything.

Will this matter to the "ruining baseball" crowd? Of course not, reality never does.

articles.title: WNBA gives Cheryl Reeve another award after playoff collapse and years of outspoken left-wing politics
articles.excerpt:
"There's been no professional organization, sports organization in America that's been more political than the WNBA. "

The WNBA has another award for Cheryl Reeve. This one comes from the people who ...
articles.body_text:
"There's been no professional organization, sports organization in America that's been more political than the WNBA. "

The WNBA has another award for Cheryl Reeve. This one comes from the people who run the teams, and that makes it worth examining what, exactly, they are celebrating.

The league announced Monday that the Minnesota Lynx head coach and president of basketball operations won Basketball Executive of the Year for the third time, tying the Atlanta Dream's Dan Padover for the most selections in the award's history.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve, who has openly pushed for males to be included in women's sports, won the 2026 WNBA Executive of the Year award. (Star Tribune via Getty Images)

The announcement comes less than two weeks after the top-seeded Lynx were swept out of the first round of the playoffs by the eighth-seeded New York Liberty, who were subsequently swept in the semifinals by the Dream.

Reeve appeared on 13 ballots, ahead of Padover's 11 and Golden State's Ohemaa Nyanin's eight. Each of the WNBA's 15 teams had an executive on the voting panel, and voters couldn't select themselves.

CHERYL REEVE'S WNBA COACH OF THE YEAR WIN SHOULDN'T DISTRACT FROM HER DANGEROUS ACCUSATIONS

That's a substantial endorsement of Reeve from her peers and it also amounts to tacit approval of the way one of the league's most outspoken left-wing figures represents her franchise.

An executive helps establish what an organization stands for, and Reeve has made her politics a major part of that job. She consistently uses her WNBA platform to attack the motives of people who believe women's sports should be reserved for females.

Her colleagues have now chosen to celebrate her leadership. That deserves scrutiny beyond a list of successful transactions.

The league's announcement highlighted Reeve's selection of Olivia Miles with the No. 2 pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft. Miles went on to become the unanimous Rookie of the Year and set the league's rookie scoring record with 790 points.

An excellent addition, obviously. But let's remember how Miles became available.

The Dallas Wings could have (and should have) taken Miles, but elected to draft Paige Bueckers' girlfriend, Azzi Fudd, with the No. 1 pick instead.

The Wings publicly praised Fudd's shooting. But pretending that their selection of Fudd was based entirely on her basketball skills is foolish.

The Dallas Wings used the No. 1 pick in the 2025 WNBA Draft to select Paige Bueckers and then used the No. 1 pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft to select Bueckers' girlfriend and former UConn teammate, Azzi Fudd. (The Hapa Blonde/GC Images)

Miles averaged 19.8 points, 6.0 assists and 4.7 rebounds as a rookie. Fudd averaged 13.1 points, 1.8 assists and 1.7 rebounds. Miles produced those numbers while playing slightly fewer minutes per game, shot better from the field and finished second in MVP voting.

Reeve should probably send the Wings a thank-you note.

In April 2024, the Chicago Sky moved from No. 8 to No. 7 and acquired the rights to Nikolina Milić. Minnesota received Sika Koné, a 2025 second-round pick and the right to swap first-round picks with Chicago in 2026, along with the No. 8 selection.

Chicago used No. 7 on Angel Reese. At the time of the deal, Minnesota was coming off a 19-21 season and Chicago an 18-22 season.

ANGEL REESE’S LATEST WNBA CONTROVERSY SHOWS HOW VICTIMHOOD BECAME CENTRAL TO HER BRAND

In April 2025, Minnesota sent Chicago the No. 11 pick, which the Sky used on Hailey Van Lith, for Chicago's 2026 first-rounder outright. That deal canceled the earlier swap and allowed Minnesota to keep its own 2026 first-round pick, too.

Reeve deserves credit for those trades. Once Dallas passed on Miles, though, the choice at No. 2 was awfully easy.

Reeve also signed Natasha Howard, who started all 44 games and earned an All-Star starting spot. Minnesota finished 33-11 and earned the No. 1 playoff seed.

Dallas did Reeve an enormous favor, and the Lynx benefited.

For all those advantages, what did the Lynx do in the playoffs?

Minnesota became the first No. 1 seed in WNBA history to be eliminated by a No. 8 seed, and New York did it in a sweep.

The Lynx had the unanimous Rookie of the Year (who also finished second in MVP voting). And while Napheesa Collier, one of the league’s best players, missed time during the regular season, she played in both playoff games.

Minnesota lost both of those games by 16 points, including a 91-75 defeat at home in Game 1.

Minnesota Lynx head coach Cheryl Reeve hasn't won a WNBA championship in nearly a decade. (Getty Images)

Reeve's four championships are part of her record. So is the fact that the most recent one came in 2017. In the nine seasons since, Minnesota has reached the Finals once, losing to New York in 2024.

During that same stretch, Reeve has collected three Coach of the Year awards and all three of her Executive of the Year awards.

Six individual awards. Zero championships.

If Reeve gets the credit for both building the roster and coaching it, she can answer for what that team did in the playoffs, too.

Reeve already won her fifth Coach of the Year award two weeks ago. With Monday's announcement, she became the first person to win Coach of the Year and Executive of the Year in the same season twice.

For me, evaluating an executive means evaluating leadership. If an executive repeatedly uses the team's platform to make political statements, those statements belong in the discussion of how she represents the organization.

WNBA FIGHT OVER MALES IN WOMEN'S SPORTS EXPOSES HOW THE LEFT KEEPS ANSWERING A QUESTION NOBODY ASKED

Reeve wore a "Trans Kids Belong" shirt on the sideline against the Indiana Fever shortly after Sophie Cunningham's comments about wanting to protect women's sports went public.

After Minnesota's Sept. 24 regular-season finale, Reeve characterized the controversy involving male participation in women's sports as an attack on what she called the "transgender community."

"They don't want transgender people to exist," Reeve said.

That's an ugly accusation to make about people whose position is that girls and women deserve their own athletic category.

And it came from the person who both coaches the Lynx and oversees their basketball operations. Her public conduct carries the authority of both positions.

By honoring Reeve as the year's outstanding basketball executive, her peers are publicly holding up her leadership as an example. Her political conduct is part of that leadership.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

The same people entrusted with running women's basketball teams are applauding a leader who talks openly about allowing males to compete in women's sports and share their locker rooms.

That says a lot about what the WNBA's decision-makers will celebrate.

articles.title: Online marketplace jewelry listing tied to armed robbery in affluent Tennessee city
articles.excerpt: Matt Finn reports on the surge in Pokemon card thefts across California and beyond. In San Francisco, police arrested juvenile suspects involved in a pepper spray robbery using high-tech tools. A sepa...
articles.body_text:
Matt Finn reports on the surge in Pokemon card thefts across California and beyond. In San Francisco, police arrested juvenile suspects involved in a pepper spray robbery using high-tech tools. A separate incident in Brentwood, CA saw masked bandits steal thousands worth of cards in under a minute, prompting the owner to boost security.

A Facebook Marketplace jewelry listing was linked to a late-night armed robbery at a home in affluent Franklin, Tennessee, where police pursued three fleeing suspects, authorities said.

Officers responded to a home in northeast Franklin just after 11 p.m. Friday, Oct. 9, and determined the robbery was connected to jewelry advertised for sale on the platform, according to the Franklin Police Department.

The suspects fled the area but were spotted by responding officers a short time later. A vehicle pursuit followed, ending with all three men in custody, police said.

FLORIDA MEN INDICTED IN ARMED HOME INVASION WHERE SUSPECT POSED AS UTILITY WORKER, 13-YEAR-OLD ZIP-TIED: DOJ

A scenic view of Franklin, Tennessee, alongside booking photos of, from left, Ivan Lagos-Espinoza, Jose Paiz-Godoy and Rubel Rodriguez-Lisa. The three face multiple felony charges following an Oct. 9, 2026, armed robbery connected to a Facebook Marketplace jewelry listing, police said. (City of Franklin, TN - Municipal Government Facebook/Franklin Police Department)

Authorities identified the suspects as Ivan Lagos-Espinoza, 22, and Jose Paiz-Godoy, 23, both of Nashville, and Rubel Rodriguez-Lisa, 19, of Lebanon.

All three face multiple charges, including aggravated robbery, felony evading and tampering with evidence.

The robbery unfolded in a community known for its wealth and high-end homes. Franklin’s city website describes it as "one of the wealthiest cities in one of the wealthiest counties in the United States."

An aerial view of Franklin, Tennessee, an affluent community in Williamson County. Police arrested three men following an Oct. 9, 2026, armed robbery at a home in northeast Franklin. (City of Franklin, TN - Municipal Government Facebook)

Franklin's median home sale price reached $903,410 in September 2026, while the median listing price stood at $1.1 million, according to Realtor.com.

Across Williamson County, where Franklin is located, the median home sale price was $929,990, the real estate website reported.

119,000 FAKE SHOPS COULD STEAL YOUR CREDIT CARD DETAILS

Police credited the Williamson County Sheriff’s Office with helping investigate the robbery and apprehend the suspects.

The case also prompted a warning to online sellers about the risks of bringing strangers to their homes, particularly when expensive merchandise is involved.

Police urged buyers and sellers to arrange exchanges in public, well-lit locations with other people nearby and surveillance cameras whenever possible. For valuable items, authorities recommended meeting at a police department or another law enforcement facility.

WASHINGTON JEWELRY STORE OWNER OPENS FIRE AFTER WOULD-BE THIEVES RAM TRUCK THROUGH STOREFRONT

Facebook Marketplace listings appear on a smartphone in this file photo. Franklin, Tennessee, police say an Oct. 9, 2026, armed robbery was connected to jewelry advertised on the platform. The listings pictured are unrelated to the case. (Nicolas Tucat/ AFP via Getty Images)

Sellers should also bring someone along, avoid carrying large amounts of cash and limit the personal information they share, including details about their homes, schedules and other valuables, police said.

Authorities warned that jewelry, electronics and other expensive items can make sellers attractive targets for criminals.

"If something about the buyer, seller or proposed meeting location does not feel right, cancel the transaction," the department advised.

Fox News Digital reached out to Meta for additional information.

Stepheny Price is a Writer at Fox News with a focus on West Coast and Midwest news, missing persons, national and international crime stories, homicide cases, and border security.

articles.title: NATO warns Russia: 'We will break' forces, destroy 'anything and everything' if you attack
articles.excerpt:
Professor Azeem Ibrahim says Russia’s heavily militarized Baltic enclave has become a testing ground for hybrid warfare targeting European infrastructure.

NATO's top military commander warned Monday ...
articles.body_text:
Professor Azeem Ibrahim says Russia’s heavily militarized Baltic enclave has become a testing ground for hybrid warfare targeting European infrastructure.

NATO's top military commander warned Monday that what he called the "lethal alliance" would destroy "anything and everything" supporting an attack on allied territory and "break" enemy warfighting systems to thwart any potential future Russian assault.

"Should the adversary choose to press the attack or commit his reserves, we will break the warfighting system engaged against us," U.S. Air Force Gen. Alexus Grynkewich said at the Warsaw Security Forum in Poland, in an apparent warning to Moscow.

"This includes not just the attacking force itself, but anything and everything that supports, sustains, and controls that force," he said during a panel titled "Theory of Victory: How Do We Achieve Military Success Against Russia in Deterrence and Defence?" on the first day of the forum.

US ALLIES NEED TO SHOOT DOWN RUSSIAN AIRCRAFT TESTING NATO BOUNDARIES, CZECH PRESIDENT WARNS

NATO's top military commander warned Monday that the alliance would destroy "anything and everything" supporting an attack on allied territory and "break" enemy warfighting systems to thwart any potential future Russian assault. (Photo by Artur Widak/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Grynkewich, NATO's supreme allied commander in Europe, also outlined a three-pronged strategy of "blocking, blunting and breaking" enemy forces, making clear that while NATO is a defensive alliance, it is prepared to respond decisively to an assault on any of its 32 members.

"If someone is foolish enough to attack us, we will fight," he said. "We will stop the attack and deny them the ability to achieve their objectives, whatever those might be. We will, in short, ensure any attack, against any ally, proves utterly futile."

The warning came amid heightened tensions between Russia and Western nations following a series of drone incursions and suspected sabotage operations that European countries have linked to Moscow.

"We stand here together in Poland today stronger than ever united in our common vision of a more balanced, more ready and more lethal alliance," Grynkewich also said.

European officials have accused Russia of waging a campaign of hybrid warfare involving sabotage, arson and cyberattacks, alongside increasingly provocative military activity near NATO territory.

I’M PRESIDENT OF ONE OF AMERICA’S MOST RELIABLE ALLIES. HERE’S HOW WE STAND UP TO RUSSIA

Grynkewich's warning came amid heightened tensions between Russia and Western nations following a series of drone incursions and suspected sabotage operations that European countries have linked to Moscow. (Photo by Artur Widak/Anadolu via Getty Images)

In 2025, multiple Russian drones entered Polish airspace during a large-scale attack on Ukraine, prompting a response from Polish and allied aircraft.

NATO launched Operation Eastern Sentry to strengthen defenses along its eastern flank.

Romania has also reported Russian drone incursions, while Estonia has accused Russian military aircraft of violating its airspace.

Grynkewich's remarks had followed a tense weekend between Russia and Ukraine, with Moscow launching fresh strikes against Ukrainian energy infrastructure despite diplomatic efforts to reduce hostilities.

President Donald Trump had announced that he had reached an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin to increase Russian diesel supplies to the U.S. and global markets.

ZELENSKYY ACCUSES PUTIN OF DEFYING TRUMP'S CEASEFIRE PUSH, SENDS POINTED MESSAGE TO WHITE HOUSE

On Sept. 30, Russia warned NATO that it could use nuclear weapons if the alliance attempted to isolate Kaliningrad, its heavily militarized Baltic Sea exclave between Poland and Lithuania. ( Photo by Contributor/Getty Images)

The reported agreement included a waiver of certain U.S. sanctions on Russian energy exports.

Zelenskyy went on to accuse Russia of continuing attacks on Ukrainian energy facilities, casting doubt on prospects for a broader ceasefire.

The tensions have also been accompanied by recent nuclear warnings from Moscow.

On Sept. 30, Russia warned NATO that it could use nuclear weapons if the alliance attempted to isolate Kaliningrad, its heavily militarized Baltic Sea exclave between Poland and Lithuania.

In a diplomatic note obtained by Reuters, Moscow accused NATO of pursuing a "dangerous and reckless course" that carried "high risks of the outbreak of a direct armed conflict."

According to the note, Russia warned it could use its full military arsenal, including nuclear weapons, to defend Kaliningrad and raised the possibility of strikes against decision-making centers in NATO countries at the outset of a conflict.

RUSSIA'S NEIGHBOR REVEALS PERSONAL APPEALS TO TRUMP AS US WEIGHS NATO TROOP PULLBACK IN EUROPE

The Hague, Netherlands - In photos, NATO leaders participate in the summit in The Hague, Netherlands, on June 25, 2025. NATO countries pledged to increase their defense spending to 5% of GDP by 2035, as demanded by U.S. President Donald Trump. The summit's final declaration states that countries will invest "at least 3.5%" of their GDP annually in military capabilities and an additional 1.5% in protecting critical infrastructure. (Handout / Latin America News Agency via Reuters Connect)

NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte rejected the threats, emphasizing the alliance's defensive mission and calling on Moscow to end its war in Ukraine.

"Putin knows that he can never win from NATO," Rutte said during a Sept. 30 appearance at the Euronews Defence and Space Summit.

Putin has also maintained that Russia has no plans to attack European countries and wants peaceful coexistence with its neighbors.

Grynkewich did not mention Russia by name during his Warsaw address, but his warning appeared directed at Moscow and with NATO's 2022 Strategic Concept also identifying Russia as the most significant and direct threat to allied security.

"My theory of victory is simple: we will block the initial attack. If the attack persists, we will blunt it and prevent enemy advance," Grynkewich said on Monday.

"And if required, we will break the enemy's forces and the operational warfighting system that is arrayed against us."

Grynkewich said NATO was already putting the strategy into action through military exercises, enhanced military readiness and investments in new capabilities.

SHE GREW UP UNDER SOVIET RULE. NOW EU'S TOP DIPLOMAT WARNS EUROPE AGAINST GIVING RUSSIA WHAT IT WANTS

NATO Secretary Gen. Mark Rutte attempts to assure President Donald Trump on Wednesday in a news conference that allies are increasing their financial commitments so Europe's defense is not all on the U.S. taxpayers. (Win McNamee/Getty Images)

"If attacked, we are ready to fight tonight, but we are not complacent," he said.

The general made clear that NATO's response would not necessarily be limited to enemy troops directly involved in an assault, but could extend to the broader military infrastructure enabling the attack.

Meanwhile, Trump has pressed European allies to increase defense spending and has questioned whether countries that fail to meet their obligations should expect U.S. protection.

Grynkewich sought to downplay concerns about Washington's commitment, recalling Trump's positive remarks about the alliance during the 2025 NATO summit in The Hague, Netherlands.

"I was in the room and I felt the love," Grynkewich said of the 2025 event.

"What I want to do is assure the one billion citizens of our alliance that we've got this. We know what we need to do. We know how we would do it," he added.

He also indicated a willingness to discuss suspected hybrid attacks more openly if individual NATO governments wanted him to address their concerns.

"If a nation wants me to, I'm happy to talk about it," he said.

The Warsaw Security Forum brought together European political and defense leaders as the continent grappled with Russia's continuing war in Ukraine and the growing threat of confrontation along NATO's eastern flank.

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

articles.title: Body found in stockyard trough confirmed to be missing 73-year-old Yvonne Whear
articles.excerpt:
Police treating death as homicide. Whear was last seen in mid-February buying orange juice and putting $50 credit on her phone in Murwillumbah

Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updat...
articles.body_text:
Police treating death as homicide. Whear was last seen in mid-February buying orange juice and putting $50 credit on her phone in Murwillumbah

Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

New South Wales police say a decomposed body found in a stockyard trough last week was missing woman Yvonne Whear, who vanished eight months ago after last being seen in Murwillumbah.

Last week, police said a partially submerged body believed to be a woman was discovered in a remote stockyard in Terragon near Murwillumbah.
