articles.title: Prosecutors oppose Luigi Mangione’s push for dismissal of state charges
articles.excerpt:
Manhattan prosecutors say murder case over 2024 killing can proceed under ‘exception’ to state double jeopardy law

Manhattan prosecutors filed paperwork on Friday opposing Luigi Mangione’s arguments ...
articles.body_text:
Manhattan prosecutors say murder case over 2024 killing can proceed under ‘exception’ to state double jeopardy law

Manhattan prosecutors filed paperwork on Friday opposing Luigi Mangione’s arguments for dismissing his state-level case in the killing of UnitedHealthcare executive Brian Thompson.

Mangione on 14 August pleaded guilty to federal charges in Thompson’s 4 December 2024 killing outside a Midtown hotel – weeks before his scheduled 8 September New York state murder and weapons trial. The killing prompted an intense manhunt but also sparked an outpouring of rage against the practices of the for-profit US healthcare industry.

Shortly after he entered his guilty plea to two federal stalking charges, Mangione’s legal team filed a motion to dismiss the state-level murder case against him.

Judge Gregory Carro, who is overseeing Mangione’s state case, subsequently postponed these proceedings, scheduling the next court date for 10 December, according to a 17 August letter. Carro told prosecutors to respond to Mangione’s push for dismissal by 9 October and gave his defense a 30 October deadline to reply.

Mangione’s defense has argued that New York state double jeopardy law prohibit him from being prosecuted by the Manhattan district attorney’s office.

New York state law holds that “a person may not be twice prosecuted for the same offense” and “a person may not be separately prosecuted for two offenses based upon the same act or criminal transaction”.

Manhattan prosecutors argued in their papers that Mangione’s murder case can proceed “under an exception” to the state double jeopardy law. They insist that elements of the federal stalking and state murder charges do not overlap in a way that would trigger double jeopardy protections.

Mangione has claimed that Manhattan prosecutors cannot pursue weapons charges against him because he had previously faced federal weapons counts. But the federal court dismissed these counts, Manhattan state prosecutors noted.

“Statutory double jeopardy applies only when a defendant has been ‘separately prosecuted’ for the same misconduct, and dismissed federal charges do not constitute a separate prosecution,” they argued.

As for the murder charge, Manhattan prosecutors insist that the federal stalking charges Mangione pleaded guilty to are dramatically different from his state murder case.

articles.title: Letitia James stumped by debate question while GOP rival delivers 'zinger for the ages'
articles.excerpt: New York AG Letitia James struggled to name a former attorney general she admired during Thursday’s debate, prompting a sharp response from Republican challenger Saritha Komatireddy. (Credit: Spectrum...
articles.body_text:
New York AG Letitia James struggled to name a former attorney general she admired during Thursday’s debate, prompting a sharp response from Republican challenger Saritha Komatireddy. (Credit: Spectrum News NY1, Oct. 8)

New York Democratic Attorney General Letitia James went silent for several seconds when asked to name a former state attorney general she admired during Thursday's New York attorney general race debate.

"Tick tock," Errol Louis of Spectrum News 1, one of the moderators said to James, prompting laughter from the Attorney General.

The attorney general's race in New York comes against the backdrop of James' ongoing dispute with President Donald Trump, who called James "a Complete and Total Disaster" and accused her of leading a "WITCH Hunt" against him in his endorsement of James' Republican challenger, Saritha Komatireddy, in August.

LETITIA JAMES' UNDERDOG RIVAL TURNS AG'S OWN PLAYBOOK AGAINST HER WITH SCATHING 52-COUNT CAMPAIGN 'INDICTMENT'

New York Attorney General Letitia James speaks during an announcement on the Standing Up to ICE outreach program at the governor's office in New York City, Aug. 12, 2026. (REUTERS/David Dee Delgado)

The pause from James drew immediate criticism from Komatireddy, a former federal prosecutor and chief of staff for the Drug Enforcement Administration, who quipped from the podium that James "only admires herself."

"An absolutely devastating moment for Tish James," conservative communications strategist Steve Guest wrote on X. "'She only admires herself' is a debate zinger for the ages."

"No, no, no, no, we admire others," James said. "I admire all of the past attorney generals because it is a difficult job and you've got to stand up."

When asked the same question, Komatireddy named Dennis Vacco, who served as the state's attorney general from 1995 to 1998. Like Komatireddy, he was also a former federal prosecutor.

James then said that she admired former Democratic Attorney General Bob Abrams, who served from 1979 to 1993.

The exchange, which came in the final moments of Thursday's debate, led critics to question whether James knew of other New York attorneys general.

"Very telling moment," Steve McLaughlin, Rensselaer County executive, wrote on X. "James went completely blank because she's A: dumb as a rock B: has no idea who any former AG is because she's not doing the job and never has been."

NY AG HOPEFUL BLASTS LETITIA JAMES AS MEDICAID FRAUD RECOVERIES COLLAPSE: 'SHE'S NOT DOING THE JOB'

Republican candidate for New York Attorney General Saritha Komatireddy holds a news conference with state GOP lawmakers on increasing public transit safety in New York on Wednesday, April 29, 2026, at West Capitol Park in Albany, N.Y. (Will Waldron/Albany Times Union via Getty Images))

"She's a mouthpiece," McLaughlin continued. "Zero institutional knowledge."

"Letitia James doesn' t know the plural form of 'Attorney General,'" another Twitter user wrote.

Nicole Kiprilov, a spokesperson for Komatireddy, echoed the candidate's comment on the debate stage.

"Letitia James can’t name a single former Attorney General she admires because she’s too busy admiring herself. She’s turned the Attorney General’s office into her own political stage and ignored the safety of the state," Kiprilov said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "New Yorkers deserve a real prosecutor, not a joke like her!"

But James' campaign pushed back on Komatireddy's characterization of James and how she runs her office.

"Attorney General Letitia James spent much of the debate teaching her opponent how the Office of the Attorney General actually works, and she was happy to name former Attorney General Bob Abrams as someone she respects,"  a spokesperson for James said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

General view of the now-shuttered Chi Phi fraternity house at 107 Edgemoor Lane in Ithaca, NY., Tueaday, October 6, 2026. (Richard Beetham for Fox News Digital) ( )

James' attorney general's office has been thrust into the national spotlight after New York Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul appointed James as special investigator to examine an alleged gang rape that occurred at Cornell University in October 2024. The renewed attention comes in response to a recent lawsuit filed by the alleged victim, Jane Doe, against the university, the alleged perpetrators, her sorority and a bar that allegedly served her alcohol while she was underage.

But James has faced calls from an attorney for one of the defendants to recuse herself from the case over social media posts showing support for Jane Doe before James was appointed special investigator.

Elaine Mallon is a writer for Fox News Digital and Fox Business covering national politics.

articles.title: Trump says he picked ‘devoted fan’ Katie Zacharia to be next press secretary
articles.excerpt:
Zacharia will replace Karoline Leavitt, who left the role at the end of August after giving birth to her second child

Donald Trump on Friday announced that he had picked Katie Zacharia to be the next...
articles.body_text:
Zacharia will replace Karoline Leavitt, who left the role at the end of August after giving birth to her second child

Donald Trump on Friday announced that he had picked Katie Zacharia to be the next White House press secretary, lining up a conservative commentator he called a “devoted fan” to be his most prominent spokesperson.

Zacharia will replace Karoline Leavitt, who left the role at the end of August after the birth to her second child.

“It is my Great Honor to have just appointed, as Press Secretary, Katie Zacharia,” the president wrote in a social media post on Truth Social.

“She has an unblemished record of support, and has been a loyal and brilliant supporter, right from the beginning. She is, likewise, a devoted fan and member of MAGA!” Trump added.

The New York Times was first to report that Zacharia has been selected for the role.

The Guardian has reached out to Zacharia for comment.

Zacharia previously worked as a spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), and now serves as a communications adviser for the Trump Media and Technology Group, which owns Truth Social, the president’s social network.

Zacharia, a California native, has been involved in Republican politics for years.

She attended Pepperdine University and served as president of her school’s College Republican organization. She interned in the White House’s office of political affairs during the second Bush administration as well as at the Republican National Committee.

She obtained her law degree from Pepperdine University in 2011.

Prior to joining DHS, Zacharia worked as general counsel at Fix California, a conservative nonprofit focused on “election integrity”. The organization is headed up by Trump ally and diplomat Ric Grenell.

Zacharia was a frequent join Fox News commentator, often promoting or defending the US president’s policies while harshly criticizing Democrats.

She is married to film producer Tyler Zacharia. They have four children.

articles.title: Trump announces deal for Russian diesel as Zelensky criticises 'gift to Putin'
articles.excerpt:
US President Donald Trump says he has reached an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin allowing Moscow to "immediately release" diesel into the global market.

He said Putin had agreed to re...
articles.body_text:
US President Donald Trump says he has reached an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin allowing Moscow to "immediately release" diesel into the global market.

He said Putin had agreed to release 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and another million after that.

"Diesel Prices for Americans and, indeed, the World, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST!" Trump wrote on Truth social.

An envoy to Putin welcomed the deal, but Ukraine's president said any easing of sanctions on Russia played into Moscow's hands and would prolong a war that must be ended.

Diesel prices in the US have doubled since the war with Iran began in February, putting pressure on Republicans ahead of the midterm elections over the rising cost of living.

The average diesel price in the US is currently $6.28 a gallon, according to the AAA, down from the record high of $6.53 recorded at the the end of September.

Shortly after Trump's announcement, the US Treasury formally issued a temporary license allowing Russian diesel into the market.

An envoy for Putin, Kirill Dmitriev, welcomed the deal on social media, saying: "Russia-US co-operation on diesel and energy will benefit the world."

But Volodymyr Zelensky hit out at the deal, saying "gifts to Putin will not work for peace" and that Russia would repay the diesel with "further terror".

"Allowing Russia to sell petroleum products is an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged," he wrote on social media.

This year Russia has experienced two waves of severe fuel shortages across the country as a result of Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries.

According to the International Energy Agency, its diesel production is estimated to have fallen by nearly 30%.

Trump has expressed his displeasure over those attacks, blaming them for rising fuel prices.

But on Friday Zelensky defended the strikes, saying there were in response to "Russia's years-long campaign of terror against Ukraine's energy sector".

"Ukraine will not set Russian oil refineries on fire if Russia does not destroy our energy infrastructure," he said.

What impact the deal with Russia will have on fuel prices remains unclear. The global benchmark for crude oil, Brent, remains above $103 a barrel. Before the war with Iran, Brent crude was trading at about $73 a barrel.

The BBC has contacted the White House for comment on what reimbursement the US is providing Russia in return for the release of diesel.

It is the latest effort from the president to lower fuel prices in the US.

Earlier this week, Trump said he was "thinking about" suspending the federal tax on gasoline, and also announced that he would allow so-called red dye diesel to be used on US highways without facing federal tax.

He has also successfully pressured G7 nations into releasing 100 million barrels of oil and diesel from stockpiles to help ease supply concerns, and previously supported calls for a ban on diesel exports from the US.

Trump wants to reduce the cost of fuel as the midterms loom - will it work?

articles.title: Kash Patel announces arrest of suspected ShinyHunters co-conspirator after FBI jobs portal breach
articles.excerpt: Jason Pack, a retired FBI supervisory special agent turned CEO of Media Rep Global Strategies, explains how stolen personal and assignment information could be exploited while stressing there is no ev...
articles.body_text:
Jason Pack, a retired FBI supervisory special agent turned CEO of Media Rep Global Strategies, explains how stolen personal and assignment information could be exploited while stressing there is no evidence hackers accessed classified FBI systems.

FBI Director Kash Patel announced Friday that agents arrested another suspected co-conspirator linked to the ShinyHunters hacking group earlier this week, as the bureau investigates a cybersecurity incident involving its jobs website.

The arrest is the latest in a series of FBI actions against the hacking network in recent days, according to Patel, who said investigators are pursuing additional leads and evidence.

"Earlier this week, our agents in the field arrested another suspected co-conspirator of the ShinyHunters group – the group believed to be responsible for the recent FBIjobs.gov incident, which occurred on a platform managed by a third-party vendor," Patel said in an Oct. 9 statement.

FBI INVESTIGATES AFTER SHINYHUNTERS HACKERS CLAIM THEFT OF AGENTS' PERSONAL DATA

FBI Director Kash Patel speaks during a press conference on October 23, 2025 in New York City. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)

Patel said the FBI is working with its partners to dismantle the group and its associates.

"This arrest demonstrates the strength and reach of our efforts to protect Americans from cybercrime. We will continue to work closely with our partners to disrupt what’s left of the ShinyHunters group and their associates, no matter where they operate."

ShinyHunters, a criminal hacking and extortion group, previously said it obtained sensitive personal information belonging to FBI employees and applicants through the bureau's jobs portal.16-YEAR-OLD ALLEGEDLY LED RANSOMWARE GANG BEHIND HUNDREDS OF ATTACKS

The group said it stole information belonging to nearly all FBI agents and people who applied to work for the bureau, Reuters previously reported. A sample of data shared with the outlet contained agents' names, home addresses, Social Security numbers, assignments and, in some cases, names of family members.

The FBI previously said it was investigating whether the breach originated within its own systems or through a third-party provider supporting FBIJobs.gov. The extent of the alleged breach has not been independently confirmed.

Jason Pack, a retired FBI supervisory special agent and CEO of Media Rep Global Strategies, previously told Fox News Digital that the distinction between stolen personnel information and access to classified investigative systems is critical.

FBI HACK CLAIM RAISES FEARS OVER SENSITIVE PERSONAL DATA

FBI investigators monitor digital threats as questions remain over how the FBIJobs.gov incident occurred and what information may have been exposed. (FBI)

"There is a meaningful difference between somebody obtaining personnel information and somebody gaining access to classified investigative systems," Pack said. "Based on what we know right now, there is no indication they have the keys to the kingdom."

A representative for the Department of Justice did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Brittany Miller is a Fox News Digital breaking news writer and former Independent reporter who graduated from Syracuse University in 2023.

articles.title: Hurricane Isaias forces numerous college football games to have changes, including a cancellation
articles.excerpt: Emergency preparations intensify along the Gulf Coast as Hurricane Isaias closes in as a dangerous Category 3 storm. Officials warn residents to prepare as the hurricane threatens the region with pote...
articles.body_text:
Emergency preparations intensify along the Gulf Coast as Hurricane Isaias closes in as a dangerous Category 3 storm. Officials warn residents to prepare as the hurricane threatens the region with potentially life-threatening conditions.

Hurricane Isaias has moved to a Category 3 storm, as it is set to make landfall in the Florida Gulf Coast.

Because of the storm, numerous college football games set to be played on Saturday were forced to be rescheduled, and one will no longer be played at all.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

In all, seven games were altered — eight if you want to include the highly—touted Alabama-Georgia matchup, in which ESPN's "College GameDay" is moving indoors.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Dowdy-Ficklen Stadium during a game between the East Carolina Pirates and Virginia Tech Hokies on Sept. 16, 2017, in Greenville, N.C. Virginia Tech defeated East Carolina 64-17. (Getty Images)

Here are the seven games — as of now — altered because of the storm.

West Florida, which plays its home games in Pensacola, opted to cancel its game, and it is not expected to be made up in the future.

This remains, as of publishing the lone FBS game to be rescheduled. Originally set to start at 4 p.m. ET, it was moved up three hours.

Originally slated for Saturday at noon, the game was actually moved up 24 hours to beat the hurricane.

The NCAA logo is shown at the NCAA's National Headquarters before the National Championship of the 2026 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament between the Michigan Wolverines and the Connecticut Huskies at Lucas Oil Stadium on April 6, 2026, in Indianapolis, Ind. (Getty Images)

HURRICANE ISAIAS THREATENS GEORGIA VS. ALABAMA SEC SHOWDOWN AS TRUMP PLANS TUSCALOOSA VISIT

This game, played just west of Houston, is actually being moved back one hour, from 3 p.m. ET to 4 p.m. ET.

These teams were originally slated to kick off at 5:30 p.m. ET, but they will now take the field at noon in an effort to beat the storm, which is expected to turn toward the Carolinas after landfall.

The Charleston, S.C. game was moved up two hours and will kick off at noon ET.

South Carolina State at Charleston Southern

The schools were supposed to play under the lights but will also play at noon ET.

Charleston Southern Buccaneers quarterback Zolten Osborne (5) plays against the Vanderbilt Commodores during the first half at FirstBank Stadium in Nashville, Tenn., on Aug. 30, 2025. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

The storm is expected to make landfall near the panhandle on Friday evening.

articles.title: Commentator Katie Zacharia picked as new White House press secretary
articles.excerpt:
President Donald Trump has chosen conservative commentator Katie Zacharia to be the next White House press secretary.

Zacharia, who currently works for Trump Media & Technology Group, will become the...
articles.body_text:
President Donald Trump has chosen conservative commentator Katie Zacharia to be the next White House press secretary.

Zacharia, who currently works for Trump Media & Technology Group, will become the president's sixth chief spokesperson across his two administrations. She previously had a brief stint as a spokesperson at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

In a social media post on Friday, Trump called Zacharia "loyal" and "a devoted fan and member of MAGA", referring to his Make America Great Again movement, adding she "has an unblemished record of support".

Former White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt, who left the White House in August, has reportedly taken a job with Fox News.

"She was previously involved in my Campaigns, assisting in key Swing States, where we won 7 out of 7," Trump wrote on Truth Social.

"I am confident that Katie will deliver strong results for our Country as the next White House Press Secretary, as she has the respect of, and will work fantastically with, the Media, the American People, and my Administration."

The BBC has contacted Zacharia for comment.

The 42-year-old political strategist is a frequent fixture on conservative Newsmax and Fox News, and has been active in Republican politics for most of her adult life, having worked as an intern for the Republican National Committee and for the White House Office of Political Affairs during the Bush administration in 2006.

Since June, she has been a senior communications adviser for Trump's media company and Truth Social platform, according to her LinkedIn profile. She worked in Homeland Security from February to March this year.

While she was only briefly in government at DHS - which she later said she left because of the strain of travel between California and Washington on her family - she has long been a ferocious defender of President Trump and his administration's policies.

In a June interview with the BBC, for example, she dismissed criticism of Trump's controversial use of the White House to host a televised UFC fight, saying the principles of the UFC "are the kind of principles that founded our Constitutional Republic".

"It's about not giving up the fight until the bitter end," she said. "I think there's no better summation of the American ethos than a good UFC fight."

A lawyer educated at Pepperdine University in California, Zacharia also served as general counsel for Fix California, a conservative non-profit started by Trump ally - and current Special Presidential Envoy for Special Missions - Ric Grenell.

In 2011, she spent nearly two years clerking at a law firm in Beijing, China.

Trump says White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt to leave post

The complex job of press secretary goes beyond the briefing room podium to include managing contentious relationships with the press, coordinating with other parts of the White House, and providing media advice to the president. The secretary also oversees an office that receives a significant amount of inquiries and requests on a daily basis.

Trump called Leavitt one of his "most trusted aides" when she left the role, saying she wanted to spend more time with her family, which set a high bar for her replacement.

A lawyer educated at Pepperdine University in California, Zacharia, 42, has four children. She has also worked as general counsel for Fix California, a conservative advocacy group headed by Trump ally Ric Grenell.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham's insufferable ex-teammate mouths off but can't make a shot, ref lowers his shoulder & Ditka
articles.excerpt: Dan breaks down the funniest reaction in the WNBA as Sophie Cunningham laughs off A’ja Wilson’s total meltdown over a fan simply pointing a finger. While A’ja Wilson expected the entire league to rall...
articles.body_text:
Dan breaks down the funniest reaction in the WNBA as Sophie Cunningham laughs off A’ja Wilson’s total meltdown over a fan simply pointing a finger. While A’ja Wilson expected the entire league to rally behind her after leaving the court to confront a Fever fan, Sophie Cunningham did what she does best: throw fuel on the fire and laugh in her face. Meanwhile, Prime Video’s broadcast panel completely missed the mark by rushing to defend Wilson, and the outrage mob on Bluesky immediately scapegoated Indiana fans with wild accusations before anyone even knew what was said. Dan Dakich shreds Prime's soft coverage, exposes the narrative push against Fever fans, and explains why Sophie Cunningham is officially the most entertaining player in the entire WNBA.

'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com.

Another Friday. We're here. We've made it!

While the left spent all week whining about Sophie Cunningham's hat and firing squad best practices, us PATRIOTS were biding our time, keeping our heads down, and grinding towards another weekend.

And now, we're here. And there ain't a thing they can do about it.

Welcome to a Friday Nightcaps — the one where Sophie Cunningham's ex-teammate, Sydney Colson, virtue-signals her BUTT off while also having maybe the worst career stats I've ever seen.

SPORTS MEDIA OUTLET CONSIDERS SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM MORE POLARIZING THAN MEGAN RAPINOE

Sophie Cunningham and Sydney Colson of the Indiana Fever warm up before a WNBA game against the New York Liberty on July 16, 2025, at Barclays Center Arena in Brooklyn, N.Y. (NBAE via Getty Images)

Seriously. This is who's telling Sophie — and white people — to shut up? The WNBA can do better than this, right?

What else? I've got Dak getting heckled by an Uber driver, a referee absolutely trucking a poor soul on the sidelines, and I'm sad about Mike Ditka. What an awful year for deaths.

I feel like we say that every year, but goodness, 2026 has been a real kick to the you-know-whats in terms of death. And we still have three months to go!

On that happy note, grab you a slice of sausage pizza ahead of Sunday's National Sausage Pizza Day, and settle in for a Friday 'Cap!

I've got no real hot takes on pizza beyond the fact that I do, in fact, believe sausage is the best topping. I'm not just saying that because of the occasion. It's the best, by a mile.

Mount Rushmore of Pizza Toppings to kick this Friday class off? Sure. Why not?!

Meatballs as a topping are underrated in the pizza topping game. They're not on every menu, but when they are, HAMMER it. You are welcome!

And that concludes our Ted Talk portion of today's class.

NOW, let's officially get the day started with some ex-WNBA player named Sydney Colson pandering to the left by telling Sophie Cunningham and her white counterparts to PIPE DOWN.

Listen, if you never speak up about a d–n thing when you know it’s impacting the people that you claim to love, care about, you know we’re fighting together as a team, sister, blah blah blah, and you don’t speak up when things affect them. They don’t respect you.

Let me just tell you now, for real, for real: For the white players in the league, when you don’t say s–t, and even worse, when you say things that are harmful, talking about the trans s–t, nobody respects you. Shut the f–k up. Shut the f–k up. Nobody wants to hear your opinion. Freedom of speech, so you can say it, but just know people are just trying to get by when they’re dealing with you.

And you ought to be ashamed. Y’all ought to be ashamed to act like you’re cool with people, to act like you care about sisterhood, all of these things.

Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham and Sydney Colson laugh on the bench during the third quarter of a Commissioner's Cup game between the Indiana Fever and Atlanta Dream at Gateway Center Arena in College Park, Ga., on June 10, 2025. (ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Again, it's just amazing. These "athletes" are just incredible. They're the gifts that keep on giving "the whole year," as Cousin Eddie would say.

As Dan Z. said in the above post, let's quickly remind everyone of the VERY HARMFUL thing Sophie Cunningham told ESPN months ago as it pertains to trans people:

"I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I’m like, ‘I never once said that.’ I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men."

That's it! THAT's what Sydney Colson, who played with Cunningham last season in Indiana, deems "harmful" rhetoric.

Speaking of last season, because I had never heard of this girl before this morning, I decided to do some Big J digging to see if her play on the court warranted all this chest-pumping off of it.

Well, there you have it. That's who is calling out Sophie Cunningham. A player who struggled to score three points per game during her illustrious career in the WNBA.

By the way, for the "Sophie stinks, too!" crowd ... she's averaged at least 8 points per game off the bench every year since 2022, including two seasons in double-digits. She's also a top-five three-point shooter in the league.

OK, let's rapid-fire this Friday class into a big weekend of FOOTBALL!

To hype everyone up, let's start off with a ref in last night's South Alabama-Arkansas State game lowering his shoulder on a 100-yard kick return:

BOOOOM! You don't often see a referee doing the trucking, right? Usually, we're watching those guys get pummeled. Frankly, it's a nice change of pace for the Zebras. I've spent all year ragging on them — for good reason. They've generally stunk at all levels.

But credit where it's due here. This guy had a job to do, and he wasn't gonna let some innocent bystander stand in his way. Nicely done.

Next? Speaking of (not so) innocent bystanders ...

So, Dak and the Cowboys put up their annual primetime clunker last night, and this was the big story that came out of it ...

Someone — boots on the ground say the guy was a driver — called Dak "embarrassing" after he threw two picks in a loss to the winless Buccaneers, and he took exception to it.

I say fair on both accounts, by the way. The guy was pissed. He was clearly a fan. Dak stunk. It was embarrassing.

Dak Prescott No. 4 of the Dallas Cowboys warms up before an NFL game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, on Oct. 8, 2026. (Getty Images)

Dak also has a right to turn his head around and get pissed. I would, too. And if the guy really did turn his head around after saying it, and then doubled down AFTER Dak looked away, it is kind of a wussy move.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

If you're gonna say something, say it! Don't be a keyboard warrior. Man up, call Dak out for his stinker, and let the chips fall where they may.

OK, that's it for today — and this week. Good work, everyone. Solid week. And now we get to enjoy three straight nights of football.

It's only fitting to let the late Mike Ditka take us home.

articles.title: Pretty Little Liars’ Keegan Allen attacked by masked assailants in LA
articles.excerpt:
Actor was robbed of his watch after being struck in the head by two attackers wielding a gun and a knife

The Pretty Little Liars actor Keegan Allen was battered and robbed by attackers wielding a kni...
articles.body_text:
Actor was robbed of his watch after being struck in the head by two attackers wielding a gun and a knife

The Pretty Little Liars actor Keegan Allen was battered and robbed by attackers wielding a knife and gun in West Hollywood, he said on Thursday in a social media video showing him bloodied and alarmed.

The Los Angeles county sheriff’s department confirmed in a statement shared with news outlets that it was investigating a violent robbery matching the weapons, block and time described by Allen on social media, where users responded with shock and supportive comments.

In his Instagram video, the 37-year-old Allen walked around in what appeared to be a parking lot and recounted being robbed of his watch outside the upscale grocery store Laurel Supply on the 8400 block of Santa Monica Boulevard. “These two dudes hit me in the head, pointed a gun at me with a knife and then took off,” he said, breathless and with blood streaking down the left side of his face and neck.

Allen added that the assailants had masks on, raising a blood-stained hand and reiterating, “They took my watch, though – took my fucking watch. Damn it.”

At one point in his clip, Allen can be heard telling someone else, “Can you call the police?” Allen’s clip also showed surveillance camera footage depicting two men – one with a knife and the other with a gun – sticking him up near the rear passenger side of an open pickup truck. The actor can be seen unclasping a watch from his wrist when the one with the pistol struck Allen in the head twice.

Allen then crouched, covered his head, waved his hands and backed up while the one holding the pistol swung at the actor again, the surveillance video showed. The attackers then ran off.

As Allen put it in a caption alongside his Instagram video, the two attackers “threatened to KILL me over my watch and would have!

“God said no tonight. My life for a watch.”

The Los Angeles county sheriff’s department said in a separate statement on Friday it is investigating the robbery reported by Allen, without naming him.

The sheriff’s department’s statement said the robbers demanded a watch and bracelet from the victim at knifepoint and gunpoint. One of the robbers then pistol-whipped the victim, “causing a laceration to his forehead”, before the attackers fled in a car with “the victim’s watch”, according to the statement.

First responders medically evacuated the victim but did not take him to a hospital, according to the sheriff’s office.

The agency said its major crimes bureau was investigating the case and asked anyone with information about possible suspects to call the sheriff’s office’s West Hollywood station.

Allen’s Instagram post on Thursday expressed a desire for West Hollywood authorities to use Flock Safety license plate cameras to capture the pair who robbed him.

While many cities of late have canceled the use of such cameras amid misuse and privacy concerns, West Hollywood’s city council voted narrowly to keep using Flock cameras, albeit with new safeguards, as the Beverly Press & Park Labrea News reported in July.

Allen also wrote in a reply to his video on Thursday that he was “def concussed and at hospital”.

Among those who replied to Allen’s video on Thursday was singer Gavin DeGraw, who was hospitalized after being beaten up in New York City in 2011, according to various media reports. “That’s so fucked up,” DeGraw wrote.

A reply from the West Hollywood city council candidate Kyle Brazeal said in part: “This is insane, unacceptable and I’m sorry this happened.”

Allen portrayed the character Toby Cavanaugh on Pretty Little Liars during its seven-season run from 2010 to 2017. He also had a role in Walker from 2021 to 2024 and guest starred in February in an episode of the Nathan Fillion show The Rookie.

articles.title: New York City’s Marble Hill residents furious after ICE shooting: ‘Why do this?’
articles.excerpt:
Locals also express fear after man shot in the neck while his child was in the back of his car

Residents of Manhattan’s Marble Hill neighborhood were furious at federal Immigration and Customs Enforc...
articles.body_text:
Locals also express fear after man shot in the neck while his child was in the back of his car

Residents of Manhattan’s Marble Hill neighborhood were furious at federal Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) on Friday but also scared after an officer shot their neighbor who had his child in the back of his car.

Orlando Perez had parked his car on the corner of 225th St and Marble Hill Avenue on Thursday night and witnessed ICE arresting Oscar Belgal, 28, after he had been shot in the neck, apparently with an assault-style rifle.

“I thought I was going to get shot,” he said on Friday The streets, now calm after protests had broken out the night before, were noticeably quieter than normal despite golden early October sunshine under blue skies.

Perez said he did not see that the agents targeting Belgal were not wearing uniforms and he did not see them wearing identification badges or any gear showing that they belonged to ICE.

However, footage of the aftermath of the shooting shows a man in a high visibility construction-type vest, possibly with a badge on a lanyard, and carrying an assault-style rifle. Bystanders can be heard on video asking each other “Is it ICE or not?”
 The car that Belgal had driven appeared to have bullet holes in it, according to Perez. The homeland security secretary, Markwayne Mullin, said in a press conference in Washington DC on Friday morning that federal officers did not know there was a child in the target’s car.

But Perez added that the car had only light tints on the windows and that ICE “had to see that the kid was inside”.

Leading New York City and state politicians and officials have condemned ICE’s action, called for an investigation and demanded violent federal immigration enforcement cease.

Zachary Miller said he heard six gun shots from his apartment on Thursday afternoon, when the shooting occurred around 4pm, just when children were streaming home from school. Federal and city law enforcement have listed prior convictions for Belgal and said he was on probation for felony offenses, with the Trump administration accusing him of having gang affiliations.

Miller said he knew Belgal from being around the neighborhood and said: “He’s a nice kid.

“I don’t see him doing something like this,” he said, referring to the accusations of gang ties and drugs and weapons crimes.

Miller has lived in the Marble Hill neighborhood – which is geographically in the Bronx, but considered part of Manhattan – where the shooting occurred for 20 years and said he had never seen such a violent encounter with law enforcement. 
 “I’m a little upset,” he said. “Why do this to this neighborhood?”

Carlos Martinez, 18, said that he had heard five or six gunshots while he was eating in P & P Gourmet Deli, which sits on the corner directly across from where the shooting and arrest took place.

“I thought the shots came from inside the store, so I was nervous,” he said.
 Coming from a Dominican family, like Belgal, and growing up in the Bronx, he said he longer feels safe at home, despite he and all his family members being US citizens.

“Over here we are all community, but personally I am uncomfortable,” he said. “They want to target the most innocent people.”

The small three-way intersection where Belgal was shot is home to about five apartment complexes and some businesses. New York police on Friday afternoon took away street barricades but yellow crime scene tape was still visible around the scene.

Another longtime resident, Carlos Rodriguez, said he felt “soiled” by ICE’s presence in his neighborhood.

“I need to take a shower and clean off the filth that comes into my ambit of being,” he said.

He said he wished that New York’s progressive Democratic mayor, Zohran Mamdani, would be more outspoken about ICE tensions in New York.

“From my point of view, he can come out stronger and more often about this,” he said, adding that he wanted lawmakers to be more proactive against enforcement agents, especially where they are going to residents’ homes and demanding access to make checks or an arrest.

Mamdani strongly condemned ICE at a hastily arranged press conference on Thursday night, as protesters can be heard chanting in the background, and called for the agency to be abolished.

Meanwhile, several local residents said they had seen ICE officers and vehicles “camped out” in a parking lot nearby that serves a store belonging to the giant retail chain Target.

Rodriguez said he suspected the agents were looking for Belgal.

Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez late on Thursday criticized Target for accommodating ICE.

A hearing was expected in New York federal court on Friday afternoon in relation to a petition of habeas corpus requesting Belgal’s release from custody, after public defender lawyers representing him were unable to trace his whereabouts, Courthouse News reported.

articles.title: Powerful 7.6-magnitude earthquake hits Panama and triggers tsunami warnings
articles.excerpt:

A powerful 7.6 magnitude earthquake has struck Panama and triggered tsunami warnings along the ...
articles.body_text:
Hazardous waves are possible in Costa Rica, Ecuador, Peru, Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Salvador and Mexico

A powerful 7.6 magnitude earthquake has struck Panama and triggered tsunami warnings along the west coast of Central and South America, according to the US Geological Survey (USGS).

The quake hit along the southern coast of the country, the USGS said. It was centered near the southern tip of the Central American country, about 14km (9 miles) south-west of the remote community of Pitaloza Arriba, the USGS said.

The Institute of Geosciences of the University of Panama said the quake struck at just before 1pm local time near the southern town of Tonosí. The Panamanian institute said that a second 6.0 magnitude earthquake struck soon after, at 1.22pm.

Local newspaper La Prensa said that across the Central American country, buildings, schools and homes were evacuated as a result of the “powerful movement of the earth”.

Tremors were felt strongly ​in the ⁠capital of ⁠Panama ​City, ‌according ‌to ‌witnesses who spoke to Reuters. The Associated Press reported that buildings shook and visibly shaken residents gathered outside as they waited for news of the quake’s impact.

The USGS said hazardous waves were possible along the coasts of Costa Rica, Ecuador, Peru, Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Salvador and Mexico.

articles.title: Thai Queen makes first solo flight in fighter jet
articles.excerpt:
Thailand's Queen Suthida made her first solo flight in a fighter jet, according to the Thai Royal Household.

The Queen was shown boarding a Gripen on 8 October at an airfield in Surat Thani province,...
articles.body_text:
Thailand's Queen Suthida made her first solo flight in a fighter jet, according to the Thai Royal Household.

The Queen was shown boarding a Gripen on 8 October at an airfield in Surat Thani province, southern Thailand, while King Maha Vajiralongkorn watched from the ground.

The Royal Household has said she is an experienced pilot, having logged about 1,188 hours across several types of aircraft since she began flying in 2010.

She also co-piloted aircraft carrying the King on official visits to other countries, the Royal Household said.

articles.title: UN says Pentagon plan to livestream execution of Fort Hood shooter would amount to torture – US politics live
articles.excerpt:
Condemnation comes amid fierce backlash from US lawmakers who branded the move ‘grotesque’ and compared it to actions of some terror groups and oppressive governments

Analysis: Plan to livestream exe...
articles.body_text:
Condemnation comes amid fierce backlash from US lawmakers who branded the move ‘grotesque’ and compared it to actions of some terror groups and oppressive governments

Analysis: Plan to livestream execution puts US in dubious company

A decision by US officials to livestream the execution of convicted killer Nidal Hasan would amount to torture, the UN said.

US defence officials said US Army psychiatrist Hasan, who shot and killed 13 people at a military base in 2009, would face a firing squad and the execution would be broadcast live, adding that details would come later.

“The livestreaming of an execution is tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture,” the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights said in a message sent to AFP.

The UN body said it had made similar statements about public executions in Afghanistan and Iran, saying they “constitute a form of cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment”.

Donald Trump has set up a committee to investigate Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook as part of his latest efforts to fire her.

The “committee of inquiry” will investigate “false statements in connection with one or more mortgage instruments” that the White House says Cook made.

“As president, it is my job to ensure the laws are faithfully executed, including by firing subordinates who cannot be trusted to tell the truth and follow the law,” Trump said in a statement.

This latest move by Trump comes just months after the supreme court ruled that Cook, a Joe Biden appointee, was entitled to remain as Fed governor as she fights Trump’s unproved allegations against her.

Last August, Trump fired Cook on social media, accusing her of mortgage fraud, which involves misrepresenting a property as a primary residence to secure better loan terms. Cook denied the allegations and sued the administration, arguing she was fired without cause.

Trump’s establishment of a committee to investigate Cook also comes just days after the Federal Reserve’s inspector general found that there was no basis for the justice department to reopen its criminal investigation into the central bank’s renovations in Washington DC.

You can read the full story here:
 https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/09/trump-investigate-lisa-cook-fed-governor

At a press conference today, Markwayne Mullin – the Department of Homeland Security secretary – addressed the shooting by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent of a man in the Marble Hill neighborhood of the Bronx, New York during an enforcement operation on Thursday.

The man was conscious and hospitalized, authorities said, but the shooting quickly sparked angry protests from local residents and elected officials.

Officials on Friday identified the man as Oscar Belgal, who they said was the subject of an ongoing DHS investigation and was allegedly involved in the shooting of border patrol officer two years ago. On Thursday federal immigration agents attempted to arrest Belgal, officials said, but he allegedly refused orders to exit his vehicle, before accelerating toward the officers who fired shots that struck Belgal “superficially in the neck”. After he stopped his vehicle officers administered first aid and took him to the hospital, an Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) director.

Early reports indicated that there was a five-year-old child in Belgal’s car, in the residential area where agents fired multiple rounds, according to the city’s mayor, Zohran Mamdani. The child was physically unharmed, he said.

Later at a press conference, Mamdani demanded from the Trump ‌administration that ICE stop its enforcement actions in New York City. “ICE is rotten to its core,” he said.

Today, however, Mullin said that agents weren’t aware there was a child in the car, but placed blame on Belgal. “He knew he had a child in his car,” Mullin said. “That outrage should be with him for endangering the five-year-old.”

He added that body cameras were worn by the ICE agents, and officials will release more information as the investigation moves forward.

Speaking today, Mullin also slammed the mayor’s comments, adding that his words were “dangerous and incite hostility”.

The homeland security secretary said that he spoke to the Mamdani several times on Thursday night, and said they mayor wanted official to release Belgal.

“President Trump actually got involved and said that we would release him to New York’s finest,” Mullin said. “If you abolish ICE, who’s going to take the criminals off the streets of your own town?”

Broadcasting an execution could cause post-traumatic stress disorder in the viewing public, mental health experts have said after Hegseth’s announcement that the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan – the former US army psychiatrist who killed 13 people at Fort Hood – would be livestreamed.

Dr Simon Duff, a forensic psychologist at the University of Nottingham in the UK, said that while there was not a lot of research into the impact of watching an execution, studies examining journalists’ experiences of witnessing violence suggested evidence of trauma response.

“Certainly if people are not resilient they probably shouldn’t [watch], but if they have some underlying psychological driver towards viewing an execution they will likely do so regardless of the potential for harm,” Duff said.

“Recent events suggest that executions do not always go to plan,” he said, referring to the failed execution by lethal injection of Christa Pike in the US. “That possibility needs to be acknowledged, and the likelihood that this would increase the trauma for viewers.”

Neil Greenberg, a professor of defence mental health at the Institute of Psychiatry, Psychology and Neuroscience at King’s College London, said trigger warnings did not routinely lead to people avoiding media they may find distressing.

“Instead they are likely to suffer anticipatory anxiety before the ‘trauma’ is shown and some people will then become distressed,” he said.

“It is likely that people who have pre-existing mental health problems will be especially at risk of becoming distressed or experiencing a deterioration in their mental health.

“My advice would be not to watch the event at all and I would hope that mainstream media would not transmit highly traumatic images [or] sounds,” Greenberg said.

Public executions were once common around the world, including in the UK, but only two out of 17 countries that carried out executions last year did so publicly.

In a statement to the Guardian, Robin M Maher, the executive director of the Death Penalty Information Center, said that her group is “not aware of any regulation or precedent for a military execution to be livestreamed on the internet or otherwise made widely available to the public”.

She added that “public executions are typically held in authoritarian countries to instil fear in the population, and to show the power and control of the government.”

Donald Trump has yet to weigh in publicly on the move from the defense secretary to livestream Nidal Hasan’s execution. We’ll bring you the latest as soon as we hear.

The preside will begin his day in Washington, and we’ll hear from him at a White House event to celebrate Columbus day at 11am ET. Trump will travel to Syracuse, New York, later to rally with Bruce Blakeman, the Republican nominee for New York governor.

Democratic incumbent Kathy Hochul is leading Blakeman by double digits in the polls, but Trump will also be there to drum up support for down ballot GOP nominees in competitive House races in the state.

Nidal Hasan’s execution marks the first time a member of the military will receive the death penalty in more than 60 years.

According to the Death Penalty Information Center, the last military execution, in 1961, occurred by hanging, which is no longer used by any American jurisdiction, and was imposed for rape, which is no longer subject to the death penalty, following precedent set by the supreme court.

The 3 December scheduled death would also be the first time in history the military has live-streamed an execution, and it would also be the first time since 1945 that a member of the military has been executed by firing squad, per the Death Penalty Information Center.

While there has been bipartisan backlash to Pete Hegseth’s announcement that the Department of Defense plans to livestream Nidal Hasan’s execution in December – some hard-right Republicans have welcomed the news.

“Public execution is what this terrorist deserves,” said Andy Ogles, a GOP congressman from Tennessee. “We will be watching.”

While there’s limited research about support for public executions, according to a recent Pew survey, 66% of Americans favor the death penalty for those convicted of murder. Digging into the numbers, there is also a partisan split too – with 51% of Democrats supporting the death penalty compared with 84% of Republicans.

However, only 39% of Americans said that capital punishment actually deters people from committing crimes.

According to rights group Amnesty International, at least 17 public executions are known to have been carried out in 2025 – six in Afghanistan and 11 in Iran.

The Death Penalty Information Center says that 135 soldiers have been executed by the US military since 1916.

“Secretary Hegseth’s comments may be simply aspirational,” the center said in a statement.

“There is currently no regulation or precedent for an execution to be live streamed on the internet or otherwise made widely available to the public.”

Amnesty International ‌Australia has urged the country’s prime minister ​Anthony Albanese to press the US ​to reverse its decision over the Pentagon’s livestreamed execution plan.

“The suggestion that an execution by firing squad should be livestreamed for public viewing is an appalling disregard for human dignity,” said Kyinzom Dhongdue, a campaign manager at the rights group.

“Turning a state-sanctioned killing into a public spectacle only compounds the cruelty of the death penalty.“

A decision by US officials to livestream the execution of convicted killer Nidal Hasan would amount to torture, the UN said.

US defence officials said US Army psychiatrist Hasan, who shot and killed 13 people at a military base in 2009, would face a firing squad and the execution would be broadcast live, adding that details would come later.

“The livestreaming of an execution is tantamount to a public execution and would breach the absolute prohibition of torture,” the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights said in a message sent to AFP.

The UN body said it had made similar statements about public executions in Afghanistan and Iran, saying they “constitute a form of cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment”.

Pete Hegseth has said the execution of Nidal Hasan, the former army psychiatrist who killed 13 people at Fort Hood, will be a public event when the sentence is carried out later this year.

A defence department official later confirmed the execution would be livestreamed.

In an interview with the rightwing channel Real America’s Voice, the defence secretary said the firing squad would carry out the sentence at Fort Hood, Texas on 3 December. It would be the first US military execution in more than 60 years.

US voters are about to deliver their first national verdict on the second presidency of Donald Trump. On 3 November, millions of Americans will vote in midterm elections to decide control of the House of Representatives and Senate, as well as the governorships in 36 states. The results could have a huge impact on Trump’s final two years in office.

Today, the Guardian launches its 2026 midterm voter panel. Our reporters have interviewed nine voters across the country and the political spectrum about the issues that matter to them, from the cost of living, immigration and healthcare to the war in Iran and whether they trust their political leaders.

The answers – highlights of which are published below – offer insight into the national mood with less than a month to go until election day. The Guardian will return to its voter panel before the final votes are cast.

Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.

The Pentagon’s plan to livestream the execution of Nidal Hasan, a former army psychiatrist who killed 13 people at Fort Hood, has received fierce criticism from across the political spectrum.

In an interview with Real America’s Voice, defense secretary Pete Hegseth said the firing squad will carry out the sentence at Fort Hood, Texas, at 1pm on Thursday, 3 December. This would be the first US military execution in more than 60 years.

A defense department official later confirmed the execution will be livestreamed, prompting condemnation across the political divide.

Speaking on CNN, Democratic senator Chris Murphy said:

double quotation markI mean, that’s disgusting. What, is he mimicking ISIS executions? I mean, I understand that in this country we have the death penalty, but public execution is medieval. It’s frankly one of the things that we abhor about terrorist groups, and the fact that the United States is doing it - I just learned this.

That is just absolutely extraordinary, galling. No matter whether you support or oppose the death penalty, public hangings and executions? That’s what America has become? Um, that’s, that’s pretty extraordinary.

Republican senator Thom Tillis said public executions were what “oppressive dictators” did. In a social media post, he said:

double quotation markHasan should face the death penalty, but making his execution public and streaming it? Beyond disgusting. Public executions are what oppressive dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan do. It should not be happening in America.

Meanwhile, Democratic senator Patty Murray commented:

double quotation markWe can seek justice in this country without glorifying violence and turning an execution into a grotesque public spectacle. What this criminal did was abhorrent and must be punished – but we as a country cannot condone livestreaming a man’s death for entertainment.

We are long past the days of public hangings in the town square. Kids watch what our leaders do and say, is this kind of bloodshed really what we want them seeing? The Pentagon must revoke this decision immediately.

And the Democratic representative Betty McCollum said:

double quotation markSecretary Hegseth’s desire to conduct a public execution is disturbing and should be stopped. The Army has not conducted an execution by firing squad since World War II and the U.S. has not had a public execution since 1936. Nidal Hasan has been found guilty of his crimes and should be held accountable for them but turning a federal execution into a media spectacle is appalling and unbecoming of the U.S. military.

The Pentagon’s announcement also drew backlash from human rights groups, while New Zealand’s national censor said on Friday it would be unable to block the ⁠planned livestreamed execution.

Speaking about the prospect of the execution being livestreamed, Hegseth had said:

double quotation markIt was a radical Islamist attack in uniform inside the ranks, and so he’s going to get a firing squad of soldiers, as it should be, and we’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public, because people need to understand there’s serious consequences for these types of things.

Hasan opened fire at a medical processing center on the Texas base on 5 November 2009, killing 13 people and wounding dozens more. A military jury sentenced him to death in 2013, and he has been held at Fort Leavenworth in Kansas ever since. He exhausted his appeals last year, which cleared the way for Donald Trump to approve the sentence this week on a recommendation from Hegseth.

In a televised Maine Senate debate Democrat Troy Jackson said that, in addition to Brett Kavanaugh, Republican Susan Collins has voted to confirm dozens of anti-abortion judges.

Republican Mike Rogers continually used Islamophobic attacks on Democrat Abdul El-Sayed in a Michigan Senate debate, accusing the Muslim candidate of being “bought off by Hamas, Hezbollah, al-Qaida”.

Donald Trump claimed that the US will not strike Iran “at any time prior” to the midterm elections on 3 November.

articles.title: Actor Sebastian Stan asks when did 'conservative' become 'wrong' while defending film against critics
articles.excerpt:
Actor Sebastian Stan stood by the "conservative" reading of his latest film "Fjord" about a religious couple fighting the Norwegian authorities for custody of their children.

Actor Sebastian Stan def...
articles.body_text:
Actor Sebastian Stan stood by the "conservative" reading of his latest film "Fjord" about a religious couple fighting the Norwegian authorities for custody of their children.

Actor Sebastian Stan defended the "conservative" reading of his latest film, "Fjord," while promoting the movie on Comedy Central's "The Daily Show" Wednesday night.

"Fjord" follows a Romanian-Norwegian Christian couple, played by Stan and actress Renate Reinsve, moving to a Norwegian village only to be suspected of abusing their children by what's seen as a progressive nation. The two must then fight to win back custody of their kids from a society suspicious of their traditional methods.

Host Michael Kosta remarked that the film could be seen as "fairly conservative" based on its themes of a religious family pushing back against a progressive European country. Stan agreed with the description but said that deeming it "conservative" does not negate the issues covered in the film.

'PROJECT HAIL MARY' WINS RAVE REVIEWS AS ANTI-WOKE HOLLYWOOD BLOCKBUSTER

Sebastian Stan promoted his latest film "Fjord" on "The Daily Show." (Rob Kim/Getty Images for BAFTA)

"Some people might characterize the themes of this movie as fairly conservative. What's your response to that? Are people overthinking it?" Kosta asked.

"I think that's a pretty fair assessment, but that should not necessarily cancel out the issues that, you know, this family is facing or that the feelings that they have and the desire that they have to, you know, raise the kids in the best way they can," Stan said. "I think there's probably always, right, on either side there needs to be an opening of the door, you know, for a sort of more of a back and forth to happen…. I mean, this is one thing. Like, when did conservative become so wrong?"

The Marvel actor added that he did not grow up in a religious home like the family in his film but urged audiences to consider the perspectives of people like the characters he portrays.

CHRISTIAN FAMILY TAKES FIGHT TO DC EMBASSY AFTER GOVERNMENT SEIZES DAUGHTERS OVER 'RELIGIOUS EXTREMISM'

"As long as there is curiosity at least instead of immediate judgment, maybe there is something else there, but if a family is trying to stay together, we should at least give them the benefit of the doubt, and maybe they are trying to do it for the right reasons," Stan said.

Sebastian Stan stood by the film's "conservative" leanings when asked. (Stephane Cardinale - Corbis/Corbis via Getty Images)

Stan also pushed back on critics who accused the film of promoting a "right-wing ideology" during an interview with USA TODAY published Thursday.

"They’re not understanding the nuances," Stan told USA Today. "I find it almost laughable to label it a ‘MAGA film’ when it's essentially about an immigrant family going to a different country and being torn apart. We could change Norway for the United States, and Romania for Mexico, or any number of places where that’s happening."

"In America, it’s going right to the heart of this divisive issue that we’re currently having, and the reason people are writing it off or feel it’s a propaganda piece is because we’ve normalized finger-pointing," he continued. "This judgmental, dismissive attitude that plays out online is quite dangerous and naïve – but it’s unfortunately predictable in today’s time."

Fox News Digital reached out to Stan's representatives for comment.

'MELANIA' FILM LEAVES PREMIERE AUDIENCE 'INSPIRED'; PRODUCER SLAMS MEDIA FOR YEARS OF UNFAIR TREATMENT

The film is loosely based on a real 2015 case where Norwegian residents Ruth and Marius Bodnariu had their five children, including one infant, removed from their custody upon the suspicion of abuse as well as their religious background. The family was separated for seven months until they were finally reunited following several court cases in Norway.

Sebastian Stan previously played a young version of Donald Trump in the 2024 film "The Apprentice." (The Everett Collection)

Though most known for his role in the Marvel Cinematic Universe, Stan also portrayed a younger version of President Donald Trump in the 2024 film "The Apprentice."

Though Stan has been critical of the president and his actions, he previously defended his choice to portray Trump despite being warned against taking the project.

"There's also a valid argument to be made in terms of, 'Well, I know what happened. I know what kind of guy he is. I see him all the time,'" Stan told Entertainment Weekly in 2024. "Still, I think there is value in normalizing people that we feel strongly about. And people feel very strongly about him in two different extremes: He's either God's son or he's Lucifer incarnate, and I think we need to bring him back down to earth."

In a comment to Fox News Digital, NewsBusters managing editor Curtis Houck called Stan's comments "ironic" given his work on "The Apprentice."

"It's richly ironic Sebastian Stan would say this after playing a young Donald Trump in an anti-Trump film that the liberal, elitist Hollywood press loved. It must not be so fun for Sebastian now that he's made a movie that isn't as interesting to these same cinephiles," Houck said.

Lindsay Kornick is an associate editor for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to lindsay.kornick@fox.com and on Twitter: @lmkornick.

articles.title: Ethiopia and Eritrea accuse each other of starting conflict after troops cross border
articles.excerpt:
Ethiopian forces took control of Tigray's main city Mekelle from rebel forces last week

Ethiopia has accused Eritrea of an "all-out invasion" of its northern Tigray region and warned it will defend i...
articles.body_text:
Ethiopian forces took control of Tigray's main city Mekelle from rebel forces last week

Ethiopia has accused Eritrea of an "all-out invasion" of its northern Tigray region and warned it will defend itself, days after residents told the BBC Eritrean troops had crossed into the country.

In a letter to the UN Security Council, Ethiopia's foreign minister called it a "blatant act of aggression that engages Ethiopia's inherent right to self-defence", following reported strikes on Eritrean troops in Tigray.

Eritrean Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel responded by saying it was facing "an unprovoked war of aggression" from its neighbour.

Fighting broke out between the government and the party that controls Tigray, the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF), two weeks ago.

Both blame each other for violating a 2022 deal that ended its civil war. Ethiopia says Eritrea backs the TPLF, which it denies.

During the two-year civil war, Eritrea was a key ally of the Ethiopian government, having fought alongside them against the TPLF.

But relations between the two neighbours have since deteriorated - largely over the Ethiopian prime minister's ambition to take ownership of one of Eritrea's Red Sea ports - leading to the severing of diplomatic ties last week.

Accusing Eritrea of violating its sovereignty, Ethiopian Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos said Eritrean forces had advanced up to 60km (37 miles) into Tigray.

Ethiopian drone strikes reportedly targeted Eritrean forces in the Tigrayan town of Adigrat on Wednesday and Thursday, amid fears of a wider regional war.

US-based conflict monitor Acled said "Eritrean troops and ammunition" in Adigrat were hit by "multiple drone strikes" overnight.

One resident told AFP news agency "there were many, many drone strikes", and that some Eritrean lorries had been destroyed.

Another witness said Eritrean forces appeared to be retreating north after the strikes, AFP reported.

There have so far been no verified reports of casualties. The BBC is unable to report from Tigray.

Dated 8 October, Ethiopia's letter to UN Security Council members read: "In this time of difficulty, when Ethiopia is left with no other option but to defend itself, we count on your understanding, support, and solidarity."

But while Ethiopia accuses its neighbour of supporting the TPLF, Eritrea has blamed the conflict on Ethiopia's leaders, and accused them looking for a reason to seize Eritrean territory.

On Friday, Eritrea's information minister called the accusations levelled against Asmara as "duplicity in their most extreme forms".

In a post on X, he said Ethiopia was "openly working to bring about regime change in Eritrea by providing shelter and support to certain mercenaries who claim to be opposition".

Eritrea gained independence from Ethiopia in 1993, but ties were only normalised in 2018, when Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed came to power.

This latest unrest follows months of tension and the launch of new alliance of armed groups in Ethiopia - including the TPLF - in September.

Last week, TPLF forces withdrew from Tigray's main city of Mekelle, which is 115km (71 miles) south of Adigrat and is now under army control.

articles.title: 'Thrill killer' and desert executioner — meet the dozens of criminals Dem AG backed for parole: 'No brainer'
articles.excerpt: Nevada Gov. Joe Lombardo joins 'Saturday in America' to discuss his closely watched race against state Attorney General Aaron Ford. Lombardo also criticizes Ford over his support for clemency in a con...
articles.body_text:
Nevada Gov. Joe Lombardo joins 'Saturday in America' to discuss his closely watched race against state Attorney General Aaron Ford. Lombardo also criticizes Ford over his support for clemency in a convicted killer's case and outlines the issues shaping the race.

Nevada Attorney General Aaron Ford voted to support clemency for several convicted murderers, including men responsible for the kidnapping and execution-style killing of a teenager, the "thrill killing" of a Pizza Hut worker and the beating death of another victim with a cinder block.

Ford is currently facing backlash over his clemency bid for a convicted killer who took the life of a pregnant woman while out on bail for a series of armed robbery attacks on Vegas tourists. Now, a Fox News Digital review of state pardon hearings that took place during Ford's nearly eight years as attorney general show him supporting clemency for dozens of other violent offenders, with some convicted killers receiving reduced sentences, pardons or earlier parole eligibility while others had their requests denied.

Ford is running to be Nevada’s next governor, seeking to oust incumbent Republican Gov. Joe Lombardo. His race is shaping up to be one of the most competitive gubernatorial elections of the cycle.

Unlike governors in most states, Nevada's governor cannot unilaterally grant pardons or commute prison sentences, with those decisions instead resting with the state's Board of Pardons Commissioners, made up of the governor, attorney general and Nevada Supreme Court justices.

JOE LOMBARDO CRUISES PAST SIX GOP CHALLENGERS TO SECURE NEVADA REPUBLICAN GUBERNATORIAL NOMINATION

Nevada Attorney General Aaron Ford smiles during his governor campaign kick off event at the East Las Vegas Community Center Monday, July 28, 2025, in Las Vegas. (Madeline Carter/Las Vegas Review-Journal)

Since becoming the state’s attorney general, Ford has voted to pardon or significantly reduce the sentences of 30 people convicted of murder, Fox News Digital found. While Lombardo has joined Ford on some of these votes, the Democrat broke with the Republican in supporting mercy for some of the most brutal killers.

Ford, for example, supported a convicted kidnapper and murderer eligible for parole when Lombardo voted against.

Michael Cu, the convict in question, kidnapped a 16-year-old in 1996, forced him to drive out to the desert, then killed him execution-style — all to steal the rims off his car. The victim was shot seven times with a rifle, with the fatal shot being fired at nearly point-blank range into his head.

"Mr. Judge I would like to tell you these people, I don't want them to be free," the deceased’s mother pleaded with the judge at Cu's sentencing in March 2000. "There's a lot of people outside, a lot of mothers outside ... I'm afraid because I have more children."

Cu could eventually make it back onto the streets after the board commuted his sentence, making him eligible for parole in 2035 — though his release would still require approval from the state's parole board.

Ford has made his experience as Nevada’s top law enforcement official a focal point of his gubernatorial campaign.

ABBOTT SPOTLIGHTS NO-SHOW TALARICO, LAUNCHING TEXAS-SIZED CRIME CRACKDOWN

Nevada Attorney General Aaron Ford speaks during his governor campaign kick off event at the East Las Vegas Community Center on Monday, July 28, 2025, in Las Vegas. (Madeline Carter/Las Vegas Review-Journal/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)

"As Attorney General, Ford has worked with federal and local law enforcement to prosecute criminals and protect our communities," his campaign website reads. "He’s gone after corporate landlords who are illegally jacking up prices, taken on big drug companies, prioritized putting child predators in jail, battled fentanyl being trafficked across our borders, and fought to keep dangerous untraceable ghost guns off of our streets. He ended a decades-long rape kit back log and has prosecuted human traffickers who threaten the safety of our communities."

Republicans may seize on some of Ford’s pardon votes to challenge the image he’s cultivated of a crusader for public safety.

While Ford offered no substantive remarks in most of the pardon hearings, he occasionally had something to add.

"I gleefully vote yes for this motion," he said, explaining his June 2022 support to make a man who killed someone in an armed robbery when he was 15 eligible for parole. Ford talked to the man, Shaquille Hazelwood, on the importance of the moment and advised him to live up to the faith the state was placing in him.

He called his decision to grant parole eligibility to an individual who stabbed a 17-year-old to death a "no-brainer" in September 2025. Ford sponsored the hearing where witnesses spoke to the character of the murderer, Bobby Thomas.

Ford also supported a commutation for Anthony Amati, whom police and prosecutors described as a "thrill killer," in a June 2025 decision that allowed the convicted murderer to become immediately eligible for parole.

Amati was convicted of ambushing a 22-year-old Pizza Hut worker as he walked a co-worker home. The co-worker, who was at the trial, testified that Amati and his friends "cackled ... laughed like it was a big joke" and jumped around while firing multiple bullets into the victim.

Deputy District Attorney Christopher Lalli argued at the time that Amati should never be eligible to walk free because his crime was a "thrill killing ... for the mere pleasure of it."

Amati became immediately eligible for parole following the board's decision, although his release was not guaranteed.

HOUSE DEMOCRAT BLASTED AFTER EARLY RELEASE LAW FREED INMATES LATER CHARGED WITH MURDER

Nevada Gov. Joe Lombardo secured the Republican nomination for a second term. (Mario Tama/Getty Images)

Ford also supported clemency for Arlander Givens, who beat his victim to death with a cinder block and was sentenced to two consecutive life terms, but the board ultimately denied his application, Fox News Digital found.

Other convicted killers Ford voted to grant clemency included a murderer involved in a carjacking, a man who stabbed a 17-year-old to death over a basketball game and another who lured his victim into his home with the promise of a drug deal before shooting him dead, Fox News Digital found.

GUBERNATORIAL CANDIDATE VOWS TO PARDON COP CONVICTED OF MANSLAUGHTER IN DEATH OF FLEEING SUSPECT

Nevada Attorney General Aaron Ford speaks about 2024 election security at the Clark County Election Department on Jan. 10, 2024, in North Las Vegas. (L.E. Baskow/Las Vegas Review-Journal/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) (Getty)

Lombardo and Ford did vote together for leniency in some cases. For instance, the duo both voted to pardon a man found guilty of masterminding a contract killing after he was exonerated by DNA evidence.

Ford’s office and his gubernatorial campaign did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Wednesday.
